text: Intake keeps the requester's message verbatim, every mid-goal message verbatim with what it changed, and one checklist row per requirement with its status and evidence; that checklist is the contract.

proposed_destination.reason: slate new scaffolds the goal record so every film starts from the verbatim ask and a checklist.

text: Supplied inputs (an original film, motion references) are copied into the film folder and sha256-verified before any tool reads them.

proposed_destination.reason: Hashing inputs at intake makes every later step reproducible and every stale result detectable.

text: After any summary or compaction, re-derive the checklist from the verbatim request, never from memory; items rebuilt from follow-up messages are marked as reconstructed.

proposed_destination.reason: A real request was truncated after item 5 and three items had to be rebuilt; the stored verbatim text is the only safe source.

text: Record the owner's calls on each script draft (trims, keeps, confirmations) as numbered decisions in the tracker.

proposed_destination.reason: Draft rulings otherwise vanish between sessions.

text: Before building, compare the candidate production routes (for example generated versus built in code or AE), recommend one, and timebox a test of the strongest alternative.

proposed_destination.reason: The timeboxed alternative found a real use (fast variants) without risking the flagship.

text: A build-gate table lists every open decision with its status in the owner's own words and where it's answered; nothing is built until the owner says go on script, look, voice and route.

proposed_destination.reason: The films stopped at this gate; the plan's pre-production sitting makes it enforceable.

text: Every owner correction is logged verbatim as a numbered direction change, then fixed in a targeted way: re-voice only the changed lines with neighbour context, redraw, re-render the range, splice, re-QA, re-mix, rebuild AE, re-master and re-validate.

proposed_destination.reason: Targeted fixes keep approved work intact and make each version's changes traceable.

text: Superseded material is archived with a README (path, what it was, what superseded it); earlier deliveries are never touched.

proposed_destination.reason: Deleting superseded work loses the evidence behind decisions; overwriting a delivery breaks what the owner approved.

text: Human approval points are explicit and blocking: the goal checklist, the source of truth, the script and later truth corrections, the production route, the voice (by ear), sound proofs (by ear), the look, hero moments, generated plates, spend beyond prepaid balances, the scope of fidelity passes, and the final review.

proposed_destination.reason: Each of these was a real sitting on the films; the plan batches them into two blocking sittings plus review packets.

text: An autonomy grant covers creative decisions only; purchases, upgrades and spend past a prepaid balance still need an explicit yes, and when a quota runs out the work stops.

proposed_destination.reason: 'Don't ping me… I don't care about the money' was said, and purchases were still never made; Slate enforces that in code.

text: Record every autonomy grant with its scope and every approval of machine use (a render machine, offloading files, quieting services).

proposed_destination.reason: Scoped, recorded grants are what let a later agent act without guessing what was allowed.

text: Parallel production shape that worked: act builders who each own their files, one sound designer working in parallel, a separate timeboxed alternative track, and central finals and central sound.

proposed_destination.reason: Five builders overnight and three on the smaller film worked because ownership and finals were never shared.

text: Trackers restate every ask in the requester's own words (ask, status, evidence), number each direction change with its quote and what it supersedes, say 'latest approvals govern', and keep a turn log, spend by balance, the delivery bar and a dated status log.

proposed_destination.reason: 21 numbered direction changes superseded one film's plan; only a tracker in the owner's words kept them straight.

text: Status keys: done means verified with named evidence; a shot is done only when built, rendered, validated and QA-passed; proofs are not completed shots.

proposed_destination.reason: A check that every 'done' row names an evidence file turns the rule into something a machine enforces.

text: Generated files carry 'do not edit by hand: <command>' and readable docs render between markers; edits go to the source and the tool reruns.

proposed_destination.reason: Hand edits to generated files are silently lost on the next build.

text: Delegate research to sub-agents with sourced briefs: a character's philosophy into a voice brief, a motion spec from real references, a capability brief where every line carries a source.

proposed_destination.reason: Sourced briefs from sub-agents were the most reliable pre-production documents.

text: Approved takes and plates are reused, never regenerated; new lines are voiced at the same delivery with neighbours as context.

proposed_destination.reason: Regenerating approved assets changes what the owner approved and spends credits twice.

text: Get a first working version of every shot onto disk fast and keep NOTES.md current: builder sessions end without warning, and one lost unsaved work.

proposed_destination.reason: Agents and sessions die mid-task; work on disk survives them.

text: Never move or archive files that running agents read; clean up only after the builders finish.

proposed_destination.reason: A folder cleanup had to wait for builders because moving their inputs would have broken them.

text: The visionary bar: every act gets one signature moment that could make someone cry, inside the brand's own visual language; correct but ordinary fails, and hero moments are reviewed against the bar.

proposed_destination.reason: 'It just isn't enough… be a visionary': a correct hero moment was rebuilt until it met the bar.

text: Intentionality degrades across parallel versions: tie every move to a word or idea, prefer fewer and better moves, judge new work against the best prior film's code and notes, and hold masters until the pass is done.

proposed_destination.reason: 'We made A so refined, but B is so bad comparatively': the second film's masters were withdrawn.

text: Process knowledge that lives only in prose (trackers, NOTES.md, memory notes) is lost unless it's encoded as rules, checks and defaults; the knowledge ledger maps every lesson to one.

proposed_destination.reason: This file exists because of it; the check fails while any lesson is unmapped.

text: Ship the data model as versioned JSON schemas: film.json, script and storyboard, VO cues and words, shots, events, timeline, visual events, sound cues, mix records, captions, QA records, joins, renders registry, validation, manifest, plate selections, generation manifests, score plans and takes.

proposed_destination.reason: Versioned schemas are the contract that lets parallel builders' modules fit together.

text: Encode the production method as a workflow with blocking human approvals: goal, toolchain proof, analysis, truth, motion law, treatment and script, build gate, voice by ear, timing, look test, kit and brief, plates, parallel builders, central finals, QA, sound and score, mix, captions, AE, masters, validation, delivery and the review loop.

proposed_destination.reason: The front-door skill walks every agent through the same stages.

text: Keep briefs in sync with what was built: one brief still said two shots were built in AE after they'd been rebuilt in code.

proposed_destination.reason: A stale brief sends the next builder to the wrong engine.

text: Generate docs from data (spotting sheets, sound tables) between markers so they can't drift; hand-written docs had already drifted from the code (ducking depths).

proposed_destination.reason: When a doc and the code disagree, the code wins; generated docs can't disagree.

text: The fast lane (a narrated explainer built from 10 s blocks with one style key, or a quick generated clip) is used only when someone picks it at the front door's question, and never for brand work.

proposed_destination.reason: It's fast and cheap but can't meet a brand's craft bar.

text: Orphaned intermediates that nothing reads (a raw cue sheet, unpaced Whisper output).

proposed_destination.reason: Nothing consumes them; slate make only keeps files in its dependency graph.

text: When a decision changes (for example where renders run), update or retire the memory notes and docs that state the old rule; two notes still sent renders to a retired machine.

proposed_destination.reason: A stale note is an instruction an agent will follow.

text: Each film folder is git-initialized for its small files (heavy media ignored) and lives outside iCloud; the source project wasn't a repo and had one Time Machine backup as its only copy.

proposed_destination.reason: Versioned small files make every change reviewable and recoverable.

text: Harvest the per-act NOTES.md files (3,565 lines) and the character motion spec into the knowledge ledger in their own pass.

proposed_destination.reason: The inventory didn't read them; the ledger isn't done until they're mapped.

text: The source films' shapes (shot counts, runtimes, voices, builder counts, render machines and status on 2026-09-30).

proposed_destination.reason: Film-specific facts; the reusable parts (pacing, leads, parallel builders, local rendering) are harvested as their own items.

text: A reference review lists what to keep and what to fix; common faults found were deck-like pacing, on-screen text repeating the VO, hard cuts, tiny body copy, a master 16 LU under target (-30.7 LUFS) and no call to action.

proposed_destination.reason: These faults recur in brand films; naming them up front shapes the treatment.

text: Reference analysis includes a table of claims in the reference that conflict with the brand's current website or product.

proposed_destination.reason: Old films carry stale claims; the conflicts table stops them being copied into the new script.

text: Truth research pins the product source at a commit, reads company code in place (git show, git grep) and cites path:line; the website, live app pages, public demos and guidelines are read and cited too.

proposed_destination.reason: Pinned, cited sources are what let claims be re-verified later without trusting memory.

text: The owner names the source of truth for product claims; retired prototypes and demos are layout references only.

proposed_destination.reason: The films' first drafts drew on a retired prototype and a stale demo; the owner ruled the code the truth.

text: Before build, re-verify every quoted product fact against the pinned source and correct its path:line; about 110 quotes were re-checked this way.

proposed_destination.reason: Quotes drift as code moves; a grep against the pinned commit is cheap and catches it.

text: The script has one hand-edited data source; the readable script and storyboard are generated from it and carry a 'do not edit here' note.

proposed_destination.reason: Two films kept a hand-authored storyboard beside a generated table and drifted; the generator pattern fixed it.

text: A treatment covers the idea as a reframe, runtime rationale (why not shorter or longer), act by act, an emotional arc, one signature moment per act, the character's gesture vocabulary, voice direction, look and sound, what the film never shows, the owner's calls, and notes for builders.

proposed_destination.reason: This was the strongest pre-production document in the project; its shape is reusable for any brand.

text: Script gate: VO at or under 2.6 words per second in every shot.

proposed_destination.reason: Faster reads rushed the narrator and forced shots too short for their text.

text: Script gate: on-screen read time is estimated as hold >= max(1.5 s, 0.4 s + 0.3 s x words) against settle-to-exit time (approximated as duration minus the entrance and 0.75 of the entrance for the exit).

proposed_destination.reason: Catching unreadable text at the script stage is far cheaper than finding it in a master.

text: Script gate: no banned word appears in the on-screen text, the picture notes or the VO.

proposed_destination.reason: The brand's banned list has to be enforced from the first draft, not only by OCR at the end.

text: Script gate: runtime within +-10% of the target runtime unless the brief justifies otherwise.

proposed_destination.reason: The target comes from the format or the reference; the gate reads it from film.json instead of a hard-coded number.

text: Script gate: no dashes in VO lines.

proposed_destination.reason: One film's generator enforced it; keep it as a default the brand can switch off.

text: Script gate: every shot carries a truth source (code path:line, website, the reference film's scene, or an owner ruling).

proposed_destination.reason: A shot with no source is where invented claims hide.

text: Script gate: at most 12 on-screen words per shot.

proposed_destination.reason: Dense text fails read time and competes with the VO.

text: A brief can pin required lines (for example a character's fixed opening line) and the script gate checks they're present and unchanged.

proposed_destination.reason: One film hard-coded its first line into the generator; make it data in the brief instead.

text: The script generator exits non-zero with a problem list and writes nothing when any check fails.

proposed_destination.reason: A half-written storyboard that passes some checks is worse than none.

text: Each script draft carries a human-readable change note in its version (date and whose corrections).

proposed_destination.reason: Draft notes let anyone see why a line changed without diffing JSON.

text: Each shot records an entrance-duration token so the read-time check can estimate when on-screen text settles.

proposed_destination.reason: The estimate needs the entrance time; the token keeps it tied to the brand's duration scale.

text: The script generator renumbers shot ids and remaps every id mentioned in the text; once any scene uses the ids, renumbering is refused.

proposed_destination.reason: Renumbering after builders start breaks their beats and contracts silently.

text: The script can declare a narrator and a character's gesture vocabulary with one meaning per gesture.

proposed_destination.reason: Builders and the voice read those fields; a gesture with two meanings reads as noise.

text: Product-truth doc template: pinned commit, the product in one paragraph, journey order, screens and exact copy, the agent or character, secondary views, the product's own motion, palette and type, live versus not built, numbers and words to get right, and where the product disagrees with itself.

proposed_destination.reason: Builders and checks consume this doc; its 'live vs not built' section stops unbuilt features being shown working.

text: Capability brief template for a product character or agent: how it was checked, sources, what it knows, how it synthesizes and explains, what it suggests next, guardrails, what is NOT true, where this film differs, and what the film uses.

proposed_destination.reason: A character that speaks for a product needs a sourced list of what it can truthfully do.

text: Propose the scope of a fidelity pass before widening it ('is this the pressing stuff?') and record the ruling: the product's core surfaces must match exactly, secondary surfaces need only feel right.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner narrowed an app-fidelity audit to the report surfaces; unscoped passes burn time on things nobody asked for.

text: The product's code is the only product truth: it wins over docs, demos, prototypes and old films, and the owner's rulings win over the code for what's claimed.

proposed_destination.reason: A retired prototype and a stale demo carried outdated claims; the pinned code settled them.

text: Keep a per-brand 'never claim or show' list for things true in code but ruled out by the owner; the script gate, the builders' brief and the OCR scan all read it.

proposed_destination.reason: Features that existed in code were still 'not true' for the film; only a list checked at every layer keeps them out.

text: A number on screen or in the VO needs a current source or it's dropped; forward-looking claims appear only as the source said them.

proposed_destination.reason: An unsourced statistic had to be cut from a finished script; a film for investors can't carry a contradictable figure.

text: Never show as working anything that isn't built, is stubbed or is off by default; the product-truth doc's 'live versus not built' list feeds builders and checks.

proposed_destination.reason: Several product features were off or stubbed; showing them working would have been a false claim.

text: Nothing is invented: every UI element, word and number maps to a citation; a concept screen needs explicit sign-off and a visible 'concept' treatment.

proposed_destination.reason: UI the product doesn't have is a claim; so is a made-up number.

text: Describe a product character only with capabilities the owner treats as true, and ground its gestures in the product's own motion with one meaning per gesture.

proposed_destination.reason: A character speaks for the product; anything it does on screen is a claim.

text: On-screen text stays at or under 40% of the shot's VO words.

proposed_destination.reason: Text that repeats the VO was a fault in the reference film; the ratio keeps the picture from reading the script aloud.

text: Script content lives in script.json, and the script checks read the brand's rules; one film's generator held its content in code and hard-coded a fixed opening line and a banned word.

proposed_destination.reason: Content in code can't be edited by the owner or reused by another brand.

text: Extracting a website's copy as leaf-text lines lets on-screen copy be checked against the brand's real words; the source tool couldn't run because its HTML parser wasn't installed.

proposed_destination.reason: 'Nothing invented' needs the brand's actual copy on hand; the tool needs its dependencies declared.

text: Hero lines have at most 6 words and at most 2 appear per act.

proposed_destination.reason: Hero text works because it's rare and short.

text: Reference analysis is one repeatable stage: Demucs vocal split, Whisper transcript with word timestamps, generation-side scene analysis, ffmpeg scene scores, change and settled frames, contact sheets and OCR, joined into one scenes file.

proposed_destination.reason: The films ran this stage as loose shell commands; slate analyze makes it one command any agent can run.

text: Every reference analysis records a method table (step, what ran, output) so its results can be re-derived.

proposed_destination.reason: The analysis had no formal gate; the method table is what makes it auditable.

text: Each brand's motion law is written once: named eases with bezier and AE speed/influence values, duration tokens, stagger rules, morph techniques, blur settings, the read-time rule, a banned list with reasoned exceptions and per-shot motion QA.

proposed_destination.reason: The motion law is an onboarding output; every later film reads it.

text: Look development runs moodboards first, then the same moodboards grounded in the brand kit, then moving look tests; several looks were rejected before one was accepted.

proposed_destination.reason: Four looks failed before the accepted one; testing looks is far cheaper than re-rendering a film.

text: The owner picks the look from a moving test; colour or opening decisions that are still open are held for their own look test.

proposed_destination.reason: Stills don't show motion; a moving test is the only fair basis for a look decision.

text: Research doc template: a source table, every claim with its source, the brand system (logos, fonts, colour tokens by source, UI patterns, icons, voice, motion tokens), conflicts and open questions.

proposed_destination.reason: Brand onboarding needs the same research shape for every brand.

text: Build the film's look from the brand's own components and tokens, not generic prompts, and get a look test approved before rolling it out; flat shapes, a 3D filament and glossy glass were all rejected before the brand's own components were accepted.

proposed_destination.reason: The look that worked was the brand's own design system; every generic look failed.

text: A brand pack defines the product's own palette tokens and font weights; logos keep their artwork colours; logo clear space and marks (registered, trademark) follow the brand's guidelines.

proposed_destination.reason: These rules come from each brand's guidelines, so they live in the pack, not the kit.

text: Brand, UI and video material goes to generators only when the owner allows it; company source code never leaves its machine (it's read in place); credentials are never uploaded, printed or written to files.

proposed_destination.reason: Company material is controlled; the owner's allowance is recorded per brand.

text: Some brands forbid self-commentary on graphics (no 'Illustration' or 'Example' captions); make it a per-brand setting, because one film tagged a frame 'Illustration' against its own website's rule.

proposed_destination.reason: An unresolved conflict between two films' rules; a per-brand flag settles it.

text: All script and research content from the source films (storyboards, scripts, treatment, product-truth and research docs, the voice brief, per-shot QA notes) is one brand's content.

proposed_destination.reason: It lives in that brand's private pack or the film project; Slate keeps only the templates.

text: One brand's truth rules (its tier words, banned phrases, its character's untrue features, excluded logos and removed statistics).

proposed_destination.reason: Truth-pack data for that brand; Slate supports per-brand truth packs without shipping any.

text: The source films' sample company, people and numbers.

proposed_destination.reason: Sample data belongs to the brand pack; the kit takes it as props.

text: One brand's palette, licensed font kit, logos and icons.

proposed_destination.reason: Brand system data lives in that brand's private pack.

text: The paper 2.5D look (cards with real thickness, soft layered shadows, ghost pages, gentle camera) becomes a library look used only when a brand's own design language is papery; the source brand's colours and signature line stay with that brand.

proposed_destination.reason: The plan keeps it as one optional look; no brand gets it by default.

text: The source eases' lineage from one brand's CSS motion tokens: the method (derive eases from the product's own tokens and measured references) generalizes, the numbers stay in that brand's pack.

proposed_destination.reason: Every brand gets its own motion law from onboarding.

text: The source films' characters and signature moments (a logo-build hero moment, a reveal, the gesture set, key lines).

proposed_destination.reason: Story content for one brand; the generic lessons from them are harvested separately.

text: The source films' reference inputs (the original film, two motion reference films, content maps, guides and captured app and web research).

proposed_destination.reason: Brand inputs; a brand pack models the categories (claims sources, UI references, reference films), not the files.

text: Split everything brand-specific into a brand pack (tokens, fonts, logos, character marks, ease lineage, look references, brand-kit and voice ids) and a truth pack (source pin, citations, banned words, never-show list, numbers, sample data, scope rulings); no brand constants stay in code.

proposed_destination.reason: No brand in the core; every tool reads the packs.

text: Brand logos compile from the brand pack's SVG manifest into kit data (class fills become currentColor, glyph groups are kept for write-ons); the source tool hard-coded one brand's files.

proposed_destination.reason: Logo data is brand-pack input, not kit code.

text: The brand pack declares font families, weights and sources (local files, Google Fonts or a kit URL) and FontGate verifies each declared face; the core ships open-licence defaults, because a brand's licensed font can't be redistributed.

proposed_destination.reason: One brand's font was licensed through its own subscription; no package can ship or link it.

text: Only generic design queries go to third-party design-inspiration services; no brand or product material leaves the machine that way.

proposed_destination.reason: Inspiration tools are outside the brand's allowance; generic queries are safe.

text: Rebuild a brand's components for film at film scale rather than importing its website code; the films borrowed the website's look language, not its components.

proposed_destination.reason: Website components are built for scroll and interaction, not frame-exact film time.

text: A brand's signature motif keeps one colour through the film and changes form only at designed moments.

proposed_destination.reason: A motif that shifts colour or weight casually stops reading as the brand.

text: A voice brief that quotes company code must not travel into a personal or public package.

proposed_destination.reason: Company code never leaves its machine; briefs built from it stay with the brand.

text: A brand's web font kit only serves allowed domains and loads online during renders; in AE the same fonts must be activated or installed separately.

proposed_destination.reason: Fonts that render in one engine can still be missing in the other.

text: One brand's frontend-taste skill moves to that brand's pack.

proposed_destination.reason: Brand-specific UI taste doesn't belong in the core.

text: A brand with no design system can bootstrap its pack with the generation vendor's brand-kit skill (palette, SVG marks, type, brandbook).

proposed_destination.reason: Onboarding still needs a look; this gives it a starting point.

text: Vendor brand-kit ids (used to ground voice and image generations) are brand-pack data, not secrets.

proposed_destination.reason: They're needed per brand and safe to store in the pack.

text: HyperFrames' translation of a brand's design.md into camera-ready tokens is the same idea as a brand pack's tokens, made brand-agnostic.

proposed_destination.reason: Onboarding can learn from how it maps design docs to tokens.

text: A private brand pack can ship as a plugin that depends on the core plugin (cross-marketplace dependencies need an explicit allow).

proposed_destination.reason: It keeps company packs out of the core while installing them the same way.

text: Never fetch a brand's licensed fonts from its web kit into a third-party sandbox; font licences cover specific uses.

proposed_destination.reason: One test build pulled a licensed font from the app's kit by URL.

text: Video analysis on the generation vendor's platform costs no credits and returns a scene breakdown, so slate analyze uses it by default alongside ffmpeg scene scores.

proposed_destination.reason: A free first pass at a reference film's structure.

text: Plan shot durations at 2.7 words per second of speech plus lead, tail and hold; re-derive them from the real takes once they exist.

proposed_destination.reason: Planning at the speech rate keeps the first cut close to the voiced one.

text: Timecodes are computed from durations and frame rounding, never typed by hand.

proposed_destination.reason: Typed timecodes drift the moment one shot changes length.

text: Whisper each take with word timestamps and snap each word start to the take's energy onset within +-80 ms (>= 3 dB rise).

proposed_destination.reason: Whisper's own starts are off by tens of milliseconds; the snap is what lets beats land on syllables.

text: After voicing, retime the storyboard from the real takes: one film had nine shots lengthened and twelve shortened with the words unchanged.

proposed_destination.reason: The narrator reads at their own pace; shot lengths have to follow the takes, not the plan.

text: Because every beat is keyed to words, a full re-voice re-times the film automatically; the renders and the mix still have to be rebuilt.

proposed_destination.reason: Word-anchored timing makes re-voicing cheap in design time but not free in render time; plan for both.

text: Shot boundaries use drift-free rounding: round each cumulative start to the master frame and take lengths as differences of rounded starts, recording every rounding.

proposed_destination.reason: Rounding each shot's length separately accumulates drift across a six-minute film.

text: Timing gate: shot frames are contiguous, start at 0 and end exactly at the film's total frames.

proposed_destination.reason: A gap or overlap between shots breaks every tool downstream.

text: An event can be anchored to a spoken word (word, occurrence, offset); 'land' means 90% of travel, and the move's start is back-computed so the landing hits the word within +-2 frames; sound cues fire on the landing.

proposed_destination.reason: Defining 'land' once and using it in picture, timeline and sound is what makes the three agree.

text: The resolved timeline must not change once any act is rendered; the timeline tool is deterministic.

proposed_destination.target: src/slate/state/ (timeline locks on first registered render)
proposed_destination.reason: Changing timing under rendered acts silently desyncs them.

text: Picture and sound share one data flow: script -> takes and cues -> word timings -> shots -> timeline -> kit clock -> act compositions -> visual events -> sound cues -> stems and mix; captions come from words; renders -> QA -> AE -> masters -> validation -> manifest.

proposed_destination.reason: This dependency graph is what slate make rebuilds and what STALE gate results follow.

text: Word timings are stored relative to the take's first sample, with the script line and Whisper's heard text side by side; film time is the cue's frame over fps plus the word start.

proposed_destination.reason: Relative times survive a cue move; the side-by-side text makes mishearings visible.

text: frame_out is exclusive everywhere (shots, renders registry, render entries).

proposed_destination.reason: One convention everywhere prevents off-by-one frames at every join.

text: Allow documented timing exceptions (a character's anticipation beats land 3-6 frames before their word by design) with a reason, still sound-locked to picture.

proposed_destination.reason: Without a documented list, deliberate anticipation fails the word-landing gate.

text: VO placement defaults: a line starts 0.3-0.4 s into its shot (longer for a character's opening line), the next shot starts 0.3 s after the line ends (0.9 s at an act break), and every read ends at least 0.25 s before the cut.

proposed_destination.reason: These leads and gaps were tuned by ear across three films.

text: Word-landing gate: a group's first element lands (90% of travel) within +-2 frames of its VO word; beat notes that say 'on "word"' are checked against the word timings too.

proposed_destination.reason: Picture landing on the word is what makes narration feel designed.

text: fps and frame size come from film.json everywhere: the films had 618 literal 1920/1080 (and 960/540) uses and 24 files with 30000/1001, which blocked 9:16, 1:1 and 24/25/60 fps cuts.

proposed_destination.reason: Every derived aspect or frame rate depends on this one fix.

text: Word matching understands spoken forms (numbers as said, '&' as 'and') from per-language tables for numbers of any length; the source handled English three-digit numbers only.

proposed_destination.reason: A number on screen is said as words; the lookup has to match what the narrator actually said.

text: Beats with no word (holds, breaths, carries) are offsets from words or shot boundaries, and read-time holds are computed from the read-time rule and the last settle, never typed.

proposed_destination.reason: Typed times drift when the voice is retimed; offsets move with it.

text: Take word timings from the final edited VO (after cleanup and pacing), never from TTS timestamps, which drift once silences are trimmed or tempo changes.

proposed_destination.reason: Pacing moves every word after the first pause.

text: Key character gestures to the stressed syllable: contact lands on the syllable's start frame plus 2, early and never late (gesture-speech research and the broadcast sync window agree).

proposed_destination.reason: Late gestures read as a character reacting instead of speaking.

text: Measure real moves in reference clips frame by frame and least-squares fit cubic-beziers to them, so a brand's eases come from footage rather than guesses.

proposed_destination.reason: One of the approved eases was measured this way to 0.13% RMS; the tool needs clip and region arguments instead of hard-coded moves.

text: Motion-law numbers become code constants in the kit and checks in QA, never prose alone.

proposed_destination.reason: Prose rules drift; constants and checks are what builders actually hit.

text: Compose whole designed objects in generous space with one clear focal object per frame; four camera variants of a thin line on a big field all read as empty.

proposed_destination.reason: Close-ups of a line or detail give the eye nothing to hold; objects do.

text: Character and particle motion share one clock with explicit per-element phases, no oscillation, and curves that start and end at rest; the flat plane is drawn in passes, nothing clips, no element crosses another, and below about 80 px the whole mark moves as one.

proposed_destination.reason: A character's per-tile wobble read as jitter, tiles z-fought and clipped, and speed jumps flickered under motion blur.

text: Big moves run slower so no frame jumps far (a page scroll on the longest duration token, a report rise over 2.0 s); tie the speed ceiling to the glitch scanner's threshold.

proposed_destination.reason: Fast big moves streak under motion blur and trip the glitch scan.

text: Settle everything out before an act boundary (marks and paper light over the last 0.6 s) and hold at least 6 still frames each side; a fading ring blinked out at one join.

proposed_destination.reason: Marks still fading at a cut blink out on the next frame; settled holds make joins invisible.

text: Motion gate: only the brand's named eases (plus a settle spring with peak <= 1.046 on named container morphs); no default AE Easy Ease on anything visible; linear only for time-based motion (progress, timelines, loaders, streaming text, drifts whose ends are off screen).

proposed_destination.reason: A named, measured set of eases is what makes a brand's motion recognisable.

text: Motion gate: durations come from the brand's duration tokens; exits run 0.75x their entrance; nothing under 0.2 s except state flips; anything longer than the longest token is a drift or time-based data; at most one longest-token move per act.

proposed_destination.reason: A small duration scale keeps a film's rhythm consistent across builders.

text: Staggers: 2 frames per character, 3 per word, 4 per row or card, 6 per block; a group's spread stays within 0.6 s and 50% of its entrance; more than 8 items are grouped; only entrances, exits and state changes stagger; order follows reading order or the data's direction.

proposed_destination.reason: Uncapped staggers drag and read as slow; the caps come from measured reference films.

text: Entrances start from at least 85% scale (never from 0); hero text moves at least 16 px or unmasks, never opacity alone; no bounce or overshoot except one documented, owner-approved character exception.

proposed_destination.reason: Scale-from-zero and bounce read as template motion; the exceptions are named, not general.

text: Crossfade exceptions: atmosphere inside one shot, a seam blend of at most 4 frames within the same generated shot, and audio.

proposed_destination.reason: The banned list keeps its reasoned exceptions so builders don't guess.

text: A spec promised by the kit brief and two NOTES files did not exist on disk when the inventory was read.

proposed_destination.reason: It now exists (written 2026-09-30) and is harvested in its own pass.

text: A mark-as-character returns to the exact brand mark at rest and at every act boundary.

proposed_destination.reason: At rest the character must be indistinguishable from the logo it comes from.

text: A logo build that worked: construction guides and vertex squares, an outline draw, a left-to-right fill, a line writing the name, an accent dropping into place with a damped few-pixel jolt, relief rings with echoes, a contact shadow, then every mark settled before the next contract.

proposed_destination.reason: The choreography generalizes to any logo whose SVG can be parsed into glyphs and an anchor.

text: A website's scroll easing set is a different motion vocabulary from a film's motion law; don't reuse web-scroll eases for film moves without measuring.

proposed_destination.reason: The brand's website had its own eases that didn't match the film's measured ones.

text: Name eases by job: an entrance ease (fast start, long settle) for type, cards, draw-ons and count-ups; a rest-to-rest ease for camera and carries; a make-room ease for short re-layouts (0.4 s or less); a snap for state changes; an exit ease at 0.75x the entrance; a settle spring only for named container morphs.

proposed_destination.reason: Jobs, not curves, are what builders choose; the brand supplies the curve for each job.

text: Depth of field sits on the 3D camera, with focus pulls keyed to the rest-to-rest ease.

proposed_destination.reason: Focus changes are camera moves and follow the same ease.

text: Banned by default: glows, light leaks, flares and glitch presets; typewriter text except for streaming AI answers.

proposed_destination.reason: Template effects fight a designed look; streaming answers are the one honest typewriter.

text: Surfaces crossing through other planes get sliced for a few frames: nothing crosses, and exits finish before entrances take the space.

proposed_destination.reason: Chat panels and cards sliced through each other in three acts.

text: Avoid pop-ins: enter from fully off frame or from at least 85% scale or zero opacity, blend colour over the shortest duration on a snap, and keep morphs continuous (no mask eased twice, no shadow or colour switching at a threshold, no label reflowing in one frame).

proposed_destination.reason: An element whose first visible frame is mid-motion inside the frame reads as a pop.

text: Moves that start at full speed (the entrance ease starts at peak velocity) smear on one frame and go sharp on the next under motion blur; run big moves on the rest-to-rest ease.

proposed_destination.reason: Blur needs a ramp; a move with no acceleration phase flickers.

text: Carry the glitch catalogue as a pre-render checklist in the motion skill.

proposed_destination.reason: Thirty glitch lessons are only useful if builders read them before rendering.

text: Speed limits depend on what moves: a multi-part character mark stays at or under 30 px/frame (acceleration 8 px/frame^2) so 16 samples over a 180-degree shutter keep the sample gap under 1 px, while a whole card carried across the frame streaked at 310 px/frame and was kept at or under about 170.

proposed_destination.reason: The plan's single 30 px/frame ceiling came from the character spec; one threshold for every element would fail every legitimate carry.

text: Motion principles to cite: Disney's twelve (from The Illusion of Life) and the twelve UX-in-Motion principles (easing, offset and delay, parenting, transformation, value change, masking, overlay, cloning, obscuration, parallax, dimensionality, dolly and zoom); only easing carries over directly from character animation to interface motion.

proposed_destination.reason: A sourced vocabulary lets any agent explain and critique motion.

text: Frame heuristics at 30 fps: 2-4 frames reads as a snap, 4-6 as anticipation, 6-10 as a settle, 8-12 as a quick transition, 18-30 as a slower entrance.

proposed_destination.reason: Frame counts are how builders reason about feel at a fixed rate.

text: No idle wobble unless asked; overshoot and follow-through share physical logic and decay to a stable endpoint; verify a move's start, anticipation, fastest frame, overshoot, settle and last frame with motion blur at delivery settings.

proposed_destination.reason: Checking those six frames catches most motion faults before a full render.

text: Material 3's motion tokens (short 50-200 ms through extra-long 700-1000 ms; standard and emphasized curves; expressive springs) are an alternative motion system for brands built on Material.

proposed_destination.reason: A brand on Material should move like Material.

text: IBM Carbon's productive curves suit product-UI moves shown inside a film, and its expressive curves suit the film's own prominent moments.

proposed_destination.reason: Product UI in a film should move like the product; the film around it can be more expressive.

text: Apple's HIG: add motion purposefully, make it optional and cancellable, keep feedback brief and precise, and in visionOS avoid sustained oscillation around 0.2 Hz and motion at the edges of the field of view.

proposed_destination.reason: Apple-platform brands and App Store previews follow these expectations.

text: Supers can use the 'read it twice' rule (hold at least max(1.2 s, words x 0.3 s x 2)) as a cross-check on the brand's read-time rule.

proposed_destination.reason: It's stricter than the films' rule for longer lines; worth flagging when the two disagree.

text: Write Slate's own sourced motion skill: Material 3 and Carbon token tables, the frame heuristics, read-time maths, safe areas, WCAG flash and pause rules, loudness targets and the owner's taste rules.

proposed_destination.reason: No existing skill encodes brand-agnostic motion rules with sources.

text: A 4-4.5 Hz wobble makes motion blur pulse at 8-9 Hz, the band of peak flicker sensitivity: any repeating motion keeps a half-period of at least 8 frames (1.9 Hz or slower).

proposed_destination.reason: The owner called the first character 'super glitchy'; this was the root cause.

text: Stagger parts in whole frames, never sub-frame delays: 35 or 55 ms offsets put each part at a different shutter phase and read as jitter.

proposed_destination.reason: Sub-frame staggers fight the motion-blur sampling.

text: The fast-out entrance ease leaves rest at 6.25x its average speed, which is why it smears under blur; character moves have zero velocity at both ends.

proposed_destination.reason: Knowing the number explains why the rest-to-rest ease is safer for marks.

text: No randomness in motion, and every key and offset sits on whole frames at the film's rate.

proposed_destination.reason: Determinism is what lets any frame render alone and match.

text: A multi-part mark moves in only three phase modes: unison, pairs offset by 4 frames, or a wave offset by 3k frames; each part copies one motion with its rotation plus a whole-frame delay (replicator logic).

proposed_destination.reason: Three modes cover every gesture and keep parts from drifting apart.

text: Character and mark moves keep acceleration at or under 8 px/frame^2 at 1080p and allow at most one overshoot per gesture.

proposed_destination.reason: Sudden speed changes flicker under a 16-sample shutter.

text: Size regimes for a character mark: full choreography at 88 px and up, unison only from 56 to 87 px, whole-mark motion below 56 px, and no motion under 2 px at all.

proposed_destination.reason: Per-part motion at small sizes reads as noise.

text: Never drive motion from speech loudness: it modulates at 2-8 Hz, exactly the jitter band.

proposed_destination.reason: Amplitude-driven wobble is the classic voice-assistant glitch.

text: A character mark needs only two curves: a sway ((1 - cos(pi u))/2) and a land ease with zero velocity at both ends.

proposed_destination.reason: Fewer curves mean fewer ways for parts to disagree.

text: A sourced survey of how voice-assistant marks move (Siri, Gemini, Material's loader, Alexa, Meta AI, Pi, ElevenLabs' orb and others) is reference material for designing a character mark.

proposed_destination.reason: Good prior art for any brand that turns its mark into a character.

text: Every engine (Remotion, AE, the web renderer, a fast-variant editor) reads film time and the brand's named eases; none keeps its own timing.

proposed_destination.target: engine/ (shared film clock and brand eases)
proposed_destination.reason: A second engine only matches the first if it shares the clock and the motion law.

text: Build the shared kit before any builder starts: brand tokens from the brand's own code, the eases, the clock, paper and camera, UI parts, charts, logos compiled from SVG, fonts and sample data; then write the brief.

proposed_destination.reason: Builders who import a finished kit read-only produce consistent acts; kit changes go through the coordinator.

text: Each builder owns only its act files and helper folder, reads the kit read-only, requests kit changes in NOTES.md and exports its act's visual events.

proposed_destination.reason: Single ownership is what let five builders work overnight without breaking each other.

text: Hand-in gate: the act's on-screen text matches the storyboard's on-screen text (picture may be restaged if NOTES.md says so).

proposed_destination.reason: The storyboard is the truth-checked text; a builder's rewording skips the truth pass.

text: Hand-in gate: body text is at least 28 px at 1080p (author app UI at its native size times two).

proposed_destination.reason: Small UI copy was unreadable in the reference film; the kit scales app UI by two.

text: Hand-in gate: both boundary contracts match and every landed beat is exported to the act's events file.

proposed_destination.reason: A missing beat means a silent moment in the mix; a broken contract means a visible join.

text: Hand-in gate: the word-lookup miss list is empty, the act type-checks, and the act's check script passes (misses and banned words).

proposed_destination.reason: Estimated word times and type errors both surface late unless the hand-in refuses them.

text: Builder briefs are layered: a base brief plus per-film deltas; each quotes the owner's words, lists inputs as generated files not to edit, and ends with a hand-in checklist.

proposed_destination.reason: Deltas kept later films short and stopped builders re-deriving rules.

text: Every act folder keeps a NOTES.md: a checklist re-read against the brief's words, per-shot description, decisions and restaging, truth pass, reuse, contracts, checks, sound, open items and a log.

proposed_destination.reason: NOTES.md held the glitch lessons and restaging reasons; it's also what a replacement builder reads first.

text: Sample data lives in one module, and a cross-shot check proves one sample company shows the same numbers everywhere; derived numbers are computed from the product's own model.

proposed_destination.reason: One chart showed 35/20/30/15 while an earlier shot entered 35/15/30/20 for the same company.

text: Label every frame that shows product data 'Sample data' (label text and position come from the brand).

proposed_destination.reason: Sample data presented unlabelled reads as a real customer.

text: Declare a back-to-front layer list per scene, each surface in its own layer with no shared 3D context, so nothing z-fights or swaps order mid-move.

proposed_destination.reason: Layers crossed and swapped order mid-move until one act declared its order explicitly.

text: Eases return exactly 0 before a move and exactly 1 after it, and camera paths use a monotone spline: values like 1e-26 marked moves as begun early, and a Catmull-Rom spline overshot and drifted a camera 274 px.

proposed_destination.reason: Both bugs were invisible in code review and visible on screen; fixing them in the kit fixes every act.

text: Headless Chrome can't see locally installed fonts (for example an Adobe Fonts install): load fonts explicitly in the renderer and fail the render on any missing face, in the renderer and in After Effects.

proposed_destination.reason: A silent font substitution ruins a brand film and is easy to miss in stills.

text: Never throw at module load in a shared bundle: word lookups never throw, they record misses that must be empty at hand-in, and per-act review entries are the fallback.

proposed_destination.reason: One missing word, or one half-written import, broke every composition for every builder.

text: The kit loads one film's data through a generated module (an @film/data alias) instead of statically importing every film's JSON by deep relative paths.

proposed_destination.reason: Adding a film meant editing kit code, and every film's JSON landed in every bundle.

text: Every frame is a pure function of film time: nothing carries state between frames, so a render can start anywhere (a still, a range, one motion-blur sub-sample) and get the same picture.

proposed_destination.reason: Statelessness is what makes partial re-renders, stills and sub-frame blur safe.

text: Each act computes its beats once from VO words in a React-free module; the scene reads the beats and an emitter writes the same beats to the act's events file, so a move, its sound and its word land on one frame.

proposed_destination.reason: One source for picture beats and sound beats is how sync is guaranteed by construction.

text: The engine's TypeScript config is strict with JSON modules resolved and no emit; the type check is a hand-in gate.

proposed_destination.reason: Strict types caught builder mistakes before render time.

text: Generate the Remotion root from shots.json (one composition per act plus review and contract compositions), with width, height and fps from the film.

proposed_destination.reason: The films registered every composition by hand, for all three films at once.

text: Generate a per-act review entry and type-check every act before any render: one half-written act broke the shared bundle for everyone, and four acts grew private entries to work around it.

proposed_destination.reason: Isolation per act keeps one builder's mistake from stopping every other render.

text: Compute T90 (the fraction of a move's duration at which it covers 90% of travel) from each ease curve instead of hand-kept tables; the films had nine separate T90 tables.

proposed_destination.reason: Hand tables drift from the curves they describe; computing them keeps landings exact.

text: Standardize on one visual-event schema (tap, type, land, snap, count, draw, data, page, stamp, whoosh, swell, character, impact, each with size s/m/l); the character kind is generic, not named after one mascot.

proposed_destination.reason: Two event schemas coexisted and sound tooling had to guess which it was reading.

text: Before hand-in, glitch-scan a lossless half-scale render of the act without motion blur and pixel-compare its contract frames.

proposed_destination.reason: Builders catch pops and broken joins before a 16-sample final is queued.

text: Make act-boundary contracts code: one shared rest-state component, specified to the pixel, that both builders render on the boundary frames, gated on the master frame so every blur sub-sample is the rest picture; boundary frames come out bit-identical.

proposed_destination.reason: Prose contracts left joins to chance; a shared component made them bit-identical.

text: When several acts share one continuous space, draw them from one Stage function of film time so internal cuts are the same pixels on both sides.

proposed_destination.reason: One builder spanning three acts removed their joins entirely this way.

text: A character rig is a track of gestures at film times, and the whole pose is rebuilt from the track every frame with no state, so any frame renders alone.

proposed_destination.reason: Stateless poses make a character safe under sub-frame blur, stills and partial renders.

text: A character's gesture vocabulary and meanings are configuration for that character, one meaning per gesture; the rig is generic code.

proposed_destination.reason: One mascot's ten gestures are brand data; the rig that plays them isn't.

text: The renderer and the part placement share one geometry formula so they can never disagree about where a part sits.

proposed_destination.reason: Two formulas for the same ring drift apart one pixel at a time.

text: A character rig exports its own beats (each gesture's landing time, size and note) so the events file matches the picture exactly.

proposed_destination.reason: Sound for a character has to follow its gestures, not a separate hand list.

text: Split the character rig into a generic mark-as-character rig (N parts on a ring, gestures, pose, drawing passes, small-size fold, beats for sound) and a brand geometry file (part shape, count, ring radius, mark ratio, rest rotations, orbit).

proposed_destination.reason: The rig works for any radially symmetric mark once the geometry is data.

text: The early single-film clock, the rejected 3D filament pass, the font test composition and the old sub-frame averaging tool are obsolete.

proposed_destination.reason: Superseded by the kit clock, the accepted look, FontGate and the streaming renderer.

text: For WebGL scenes, an accumulation renderer (lens-disk camera jitter with a sheared frustum for depth of field, Halton anti-aliasing) gives deterministic per-frame depth of field.

proposed_destination.reason: Useful only if a brand's look calls for 3D; kept as a technique, not a default.

text: @react-three/postprocessing renders blank under Remotion's manual frame loop.

proposed_destination.reason: A 3D look that relies on post effects needs another path.

text: The kit's theme comes from the brand pack as semantic roles (page, surface, ink levels, gray ramp, accent ramp, inverse, soft accent) plus status tones; light and dark grounds derive from the theme, and no colour literal lives outside it.

proposed_destination.reason: The source kit had 65 colour literals and 23 hex values outside its token file.

text: Measure text with canvas metrics on the loaded brand font (never a hard-coded family) so layouts fit before render.

proposed_destination.reason: The source measured with one brand's family name in 40 places.

text: LogoBuild takes a parsed logo spec: paths, per-glyph boxes computed from path bounding boxes (not a hand-measured table), a designated anchor element, construction guides from the bounding-box edges, and the anchor colour from the artwork.

proposed_destination.reason: The source logo build asserted one wordmark's exact path count and hand-measured boxes.

text: Sample data, chart parameters and product copy live in per-film content modules; kit components take them as props.

proposed_destination.reason: Content baked into kit components can't serve a second brand.

text: The kit's settle spring (damping ratio 0.7, natural frequency 9.5, peak about 1.046) is forced to exactly 1 by the end of its duration.

proposed_destination.reason: A spring that never quite arrives leaves a residual wobble at the next contract.

text: Paper-card technique: thickness as a stack of silhouettes 1.6 px apart (so rounded corners keep their edge), ghost pages in the card's own space, opacity and filters on leaves only, a CSS-perspective camera centred on the frame, and paper grain as fractal noise (multiply about 5% on light, soft-light about 12% on dark).

proposed_destination.reason: The technique belongs to the optional paper look, not to every brand.

text: The film type scale (hero, statement, headings, body, small, eyebrow, mono and large numerals at 1080p) comes from the brand pack and scales with frame height.

proposed_destination.reason: The source scale was bound to one brand's font and ink.

text: A generic Art component renders any brand SVG by key, with Logo, Mark and Icon built on it.

proposed_destination.reason: Brand-named components in the kit become generic keyed ones.

text: Chart components are parametric: a distribution chart takes mean, standard deviation, range and labels as props, and a radar chart takes its spokes; the source hard-coded one product's scale.

proposed_destination.reason: Charts are reusable only when their data is.

text: App UI primitives (surface, eyebrow, hairline, button, checkbox, field, chip, pill, status, progress, avatar) are styled from the theme; product-specific semantics stay in the brand's content module.

proposed_destination.reason: The primitives are generic once the brand's semantics move out.

text: Shared named places (a surface's home position, a corner, an avatar spot) let builders hand objects across act boundaries at exact coordinates.

proposed_destination.reason: Hand-offs between builders work when both use the same named coordinates.

text: Kit components never import from act scene files; shared surfaces move into the kit.

proposed_destination.reason: The source kit reached into two films' scene files for its report surfaces.

text: An AI-assistant chat surface is a reusable kit part: an avatar that becomes an input island, full chat, a chip that morphs continuously into a sent bubble, a streaming answer with token slots, a working label and follow-up chips; the copy comes from the brand.

proposed_destination.reason: Many product films show an assistant; the surface generalizes under brand copy.

text: A printed-page face (warm paper) is a reusable kit surface.

proposed_destination.reason: Printed collateral appears in product stories often enough to keep the idea.

text: Each act folder follows one pattern: an index (ActRoot plus scene), a beats module computing every beat from words, scene files per shot or world, an events emitter, NOTES.md, and optionally a review-only entry.

proposed_destination.reason: A shared shape lets any builder pick up another's act.

text: The kit camera is a look-at 2.5D camera whose dolly interpolates in z, not scale, with moves evaluated at time t and a project() helper for placing objects.

proposed_destination.reason: Scale-based dollies distort perspective; z-dollies read as real camera moves.

text: Ship a one-frame kit proof sheet (a gallery of every kit component) as a review composition.

proposed_destination.reason: A kit is reviewed by eye before builders use it.

text: Draw textured objects (grain, ink) at one base size and scale the result, so the texture never jumps as the object scales.

proposed_destination.reason: A medallion's grain jumped until it was drawn once at a fixed size.

text: A two-sided paper card with edge slices can flip without showing a missing edge.

proposed_destination.reason: A flipping card is a common paper-look move; the technique avoids a hollow edge.

text: Audit the kit for repeated components now and then, using a repeats register.

proposed_destination.reason: The website's audit method caught duplicates; the kit had 22 emitters and 9 T90 tables before anyone counted.

text: Use only the font weights the product ships, and tabular figures on every number.

proposed_destination.reason: Extra weights break the brand; proportional digits jitter in count-ups.

text: Reveal hero lines per character (rise about 24 px, opacity from 0, blur 6 to 0 on the entrance ease), other lines per word and lists per line.

proposed_destination.reason: The reveal hierarchy keeps the eye on what matters.

text: Count-ups use the entrance ease (never linear), tabular figures and real values only; each figure holds at least 3 frames so digits tick without flicker, and a value already on screen is never counted again.

proposed_destination.reason: A second count-up of a value on screen read as a glitch.

text: Path morphs resample both shapes to equal vertex counts (64) with the first vertex at the same anchor (the left-most point).

proposed_destination.reason: Unequal vertex counts or anchors make morphs twist.

text: Opacity or a filter on a preserve-3d element flattens it, and a translucent card shows its grey thickness layers through its face: put opacity and blur on leaves, and fade a card as one flat sheet.

proposed_destination.reason: Grey layers showing through a fading card read as a render bug.

text: Parts placed in 3D inside a tilted preserve-3d group z-fight under the 16-sample shutter; draw character rigs as one flat plane in passes.

proposed_destination.reason: A character's tiles flickered until the rig went flat.

text: CSS clip-path: path() silently fails in headless Chrome and SVG data-URI masks can decode after the screenshot: use polygon() clips and CSS mask-image gradients.

proposed_destination.reason: Both failures are silent in headless renders.

text: A clip-path on a transformed element rides its transform: clip on untransformed full-frame wrappers.

proposed_destination.reason: A corner switched at the wrong height because its clip moved with the element.

text: Zero-length dashed SVG strokes still paint a dot; guard zero-length strokes.

proposed_destination.reason: Specks appeared before a logo's construction began.

text: Huge translateZ zooms rasterise badly: use a 2D camera over poses with zoom in log space.

proposed_destination.reason: A 25x translateZ zoom rasterised visibly.

text: CSS transforms change the raster (shadows shift up to 3 levels), so 'same picture' isn't 'same pixels': draw rest states with no transform and pixel-diff contract frames.

proposed_destination.reason: A ring at 90 degrees and at 0 degrees looked the same and diffed differently.

text: Parallel builders overwrite each other's scratch files: give each builder its own scratch folder.

proposed_destination.reason: Another agent overwrote a builder's contact-sheet script mid-session.

text: Positioned type inside a zero-width container wraps one word per line: set white-space: nowrap on positioned type.

proposed_destination.reason: A headline broke into a word per line inside a world container.

text: One React-free clock module is used by both scenes and event emitters; the films had seven re-implemented clocks.

proposed_destination.reason: A kit fix never reaches acts that carry their own copy.

text: One emit-events command bundles any act's beats and validates kinds, sizes, span, unique ids and one impact per act; the films had 22 separate emitters, each stubbing fonts to run in Node.

proposed_destination.reason: Duplicated emitters drift; one validated command makes the events contract enforceable.

text: The kit's per-character type caps its group spread at 0.6 s; three acts re-implemented the cap because the kit lacked it.

proposed_destination.reason: A long headline revealed per character drags without the cap.

text: One chain() helper moves values through steps from wherever they were (world poses, cameras, objects).

proposed_destination.reason: Three versions of the same helper existed across acts.

text: Promote the proven per-act helpers into the kit: fade-as-one-sheet, monotone spline, text measurement, streaming text with token slots, press and bump, and the declared stacking stage.

proposed_destination.reason: Helpers that stay in acts get re-invented; a kit fix then misses them.

text: Kit modules: theme, fonts (FontGate), clock (React-free, one film, never-throw lookups), motion (exact eases, tokens, staggers, startFor, chain, monotone spline, settle), paper (card, fade card, look-at camera, world layer, ground, grain), type (capped per-char, per-word, arrive, count-up), charts, UI primitives, logo build, character rig, chat surface, contracts and review sheets.

proposed_destination.reason: The module list is the builder's map of what already exists.

text: Shot-recipe cards with motion previews (video-shotcraft) are prior art for kit review sheets; Remotion's licence still applies to them.

proposed_destination.reason: Review sheets are how a kit gets approved by eye.

text: Draw a multi-part mark as two fixed sheets with opacity and shadow per sheet, never per part; render flat and tilt the layer.

proposed_destination.reason: Per-part paint order showed seams, double shadows and z-fighting.

text: Keep a clear circle of 0.85 of the mark's diameter inside every clipping box, so no part ever clips.

proposed_destination.reason: Clipped parts were one of the original character glitches.

text: A character's sound contract is one visual-events row per note with t = frame / fps exactly; the sound engine adds no offsets.

proposed_destination.reason: Offsets added downstream are how picture and sound drift apart.

text: Character rigs pass automated acceptance tests (determinism, calm at rest, symmetry per sub-sample, speed, frequency, split point, clipping, sound timing) plus a review by eye of the gesture sheet at small and large sizes.

proposed_destination.reason: The spec's nine tests turn a motion law into something a machine enforces.

text: Every act renders from day one through a placeholder (page, act and shot id, on-screen text, VO, the sample-data label and the character at rest) that keeps the act's export name and props, so the film renders end to end while builders work.

proposed_destination.reason: Three builders worked in parallel on a film that always rendered.

text: Every kit gets a review sheet checked by eye before builders use it: a gesture sheet with each gesture in its own cell from t = 1 s, shared surfaces at rest in frame, and look tests on alternative grounds.

proposed_destination.reason: A kit error caught on a sheet costs minutes; caught in five acts it costs a night.

text: The kit's public API is one barrel module.

proposed_destination.reason: Builders import from one place, and the surface is easy to review.

text: Per-character type animated outside a browser needs real glyph offsets (HarfBuzz shaping) to keep kerning.

proposed_destination.reason: Naive per-character placement breaks kerning and looks cheap.

text: Cross-check disputed transcript lines with a second Whisper model before trusting them.

proposed_destination.reason: One model's mishearing becomes a wrong script line; two models agreeing is cheap insurance.

text: Cast a narrator with a shootout: the same line across engines and voices, loudness-matched into one labelled reel, checked against a public TTS ranking, and picked by the owner by ear.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner chose by ear from a reel; proxies and rankings only narrow the field.

text: Voice each line with its neighbouring lines passed as previous and next text; keep existing takes unless forced.

proposed_destination.reason: Neighbour context keeps delivery continuous, and keeping takes protects approved work.

text: Voice gate: every read fits its shot, starting the lead time in and ending at least the tail time before the cut.

proposed_destination.reason: A read that spills past the cut breaks sync and the next line.

text: Voice gate: Whisper hears every line word for word; the only accepted differences are digits versus spelled numbers and spelling variants.

proposed_destination.reason: Catches dropped, doubled or misread words before they reach the mix.

text: Research the current TTS model's expressive tags and check the best models against the live API at project start; tag sparingly and A/B a handful of key lines for the owner before re-voicing everything.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner asked for tags after all takes were voiced; the A/B on a few lines is what makes that request safe and cheap.

text: A VO cue can carry a duration that trims the take, used to cut a leaked next-line onset without regenerating the take.

proposed_destination.reason: Trimming a cue is free and keeps the approved take; regenerating costs credits and changes the read.

text: Take VO text from Whisper with a second model agreeing, and use generation-side video analysis only for segmentation and visual notes; its per-scene 'audio' field paraphrased on-screen text instead of the voice.

proposed_destination.reason: Trusting the analysis field would have put on-screen text into the reference transcript.

text: Check brand-word pronunciation by transcription on every take and on the final mix: one engine clipped the brand name while another said it in full.

proposed_destination.reason: A clipped brand name is the one mistake a brand film can't ship.

text: Context-conditioned TTS can leak the next line's onset into a take's tail (the owner heard it at 1:28): scan every take's tail for sound after silence and trim after the last word decays; never regenerate an approved take for this.

proposed_destination.reason: Previous/next text improves continuity but invites the leak; the scan catches it before the owner does.

text: ElevenLabs' speed setting barely moves eleven_v4 (13.28 s at 1.0, 12.80 s at 1.06, 13.52 s at 1.1): pace in post by keeping interior pauses over 0.25 s at 80% (cut from the middle), then Rubber Band R3 tempo 1.06 with formants kept, then re-check with Whisper.

proposed_destination.reason: Take-to-take variation exceeds the setting; post pacing was approved by ear on two films.

text: Designed voices can perform differently on the production TTS model (higher pitch, faster than the previews): render candidates on the production model before choosing, rank on measured proxies and let the owner pick by ear.

proposed_destination.reason: Previews are made on the design model; the film is voiced on another.

text: A designed voice can carry a baked-in buzz (5-12 kHz, present even in lossless PCM; the isolator lowered it only about 2 dB): offer 3-5 labelled cleanup variants and let the owner pick by ear.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner picked a gentle denoise plus expander from five options; no single default was right.

text: The source films' voice ids and brand-kit id.

proposed_destination.reason: Account-bound ids for one brand; they go in that brand's VoiceProfile, never in the core.

text: Voice tools read the voice id, model and output folder from the brand's VoiceProfile, not a default narrator.

proposed_destination.reason: Defaults to one narrator's id leaked into every tool.

text: Voice design runs brief -> prompts -> seeded design passes (3 previews a call, seeds x guidance) -> Whisper and measured proxies -> ranking -> save the best per prompt -> render on the production model -> the owner picks by ear.

proposed_destination.reason: Each step filters; only the last one decides, and it's a person listening.

text: Voice cleanup starts with a diagnosis (mp3 against lossless PCM against the Voice Isolator, measuring speech level against the gap floor), then offers Voice Remix variants and a DSP chain (afftdn tracking the measured floor plus a gentle agate expander).

proposed_destination.reason: The diagnosis proved the floor was in the voice, not the codec, which decided the fix.

text: Captions take their text from the script and their timing from the words: align script to heard tokens (so '2,500' matches 'twenty-five hundred'), chunk at sentences then clauses, wrap balanced lines that prefer breaks before joining words, end 40 ms before the next cue, fold one- or two-word flashes into neighbours, and flag cues under 0.8 s.

proposed_destination.reason: Script text plus spoken timing gives captions that are exact and readable.

text: Casting reels loudness-match every take (about -20 LUFS) with a labelled title card and a short gap, so the owner compares voices, not volume.

proposed_destination.reason: Louder takes win blind comparisons; matching removes that bias.

text: Character voice brief template: who they are, values each with a source, how they speak (warmth, pace, breath lengths at full stops and turns, pitch register, delivery per sentence type, the opening line, mic and room), what they never sound like, a philosophy-to-sound table, model choice, prompts, preview text, measured comparison, candidates, the production-model check, recommendation and credits.

proposed_destination.reason: The strongest character-voice document in the project; its structure is generic.

text: Voice Design runs a few seeded passes at different guidance scales (for example 3.5, 5.0 and 7.0) over each prompt; 9 calls gave 27 previews.

proposed_destination.reason: Seeds and guidance are the useful levers; more passes add cost faster than quality.

text: Voice Design requests set should_enhance off, log each preview's generated_voice_id and cost headers, and detect quota errors explicitly.

proposed_destination.reason: Enhancement rewrites the description; logging ids is how a preview is saved later.

text: Voice proxy targets for a narrating character (defaults to tune per voice): 150-170 wpm, mean sentence pause 0.35-0.7 s (minimum 0.12 s), pitch range 9.5-13 semitones, statements ending on a fall of at least 1 semitone with no rise over 1.5, a pause floor at or below -75 dBFS, and zero word errors including brand words.

proposed_destination.reason: Proxies filter 27 previews to a few; the owner still picks by ear.

text: Rank previews on a weighted proxy score: words and pace weigh most, then endings, breathing, range, cleanliness, lift, voicing, pitch fit and confidence.

proposed_destination.reason: Weights encode what the brief cares about most.

text: Voice Remix can clean a recording without changing the voice (prompt strength 0.25-0.5 across a few seeds, lossless output, a description that says 'keep this exact voice, change only the recording').

proposed_destination.reason: One of the cleanup options offered to the owner; DSP won that time.

text: Request lossless PCM (pcm_48000) when the plan allows and fall back to pcm_44100 on a 400, 403 or 422; keep raw, cleaned and paced versions of every take.

proposed_destination.reason: Lossless takes survive cleanup and pacing; keeping every stage lets any step be redone.

text: The approved cleanup chain was afftdn (nr 18, nf -64, noise tracking on) then a gentle agate (threshold 0.004, ratio 2.5, attack 4 ms, release 180 ms, range 0.06), output 48 kHz / 24-bit; it's a starting point, and each voice gets its own pick by ear.

proposed_destination.reason: The chain is recorded byte for byte so a re-voice sounds like the approved takes.

text: ElevenLabs output format depends on plan: mp3_44100_192 needs Creator or above, and PCM needs Pro.

proposed_destination.reason: Lossless voice silently isn't available on smaller plans; doctor reports the plan.

text: Voice Design charges once per call for the preview text (about 546 characters a call), and saved voices use library slots (160 on Pro).

proposed_destination.reason: Design is cheap per call but slots run out if every preview is saved.

text: Narration goes to ElevenLabs direct: the generation vendor's TTS route gave 128 kbps against 192 and allowed about 4 jobs at once (a fifth hit 429), and its default audio model clipped the brand word.

proposed_destination.reason: Routing narration to the voice vendor is a quality decision, not a cost one.

text: Voice ids are account-bound: designed voices live in one account and library voices must be added per account, so a brand's VoiceProfile records the account too.

proposed_destination.reason: A voice id copied to another account simply fails.

text: Never ship audio of a brand's character voice as a demo.

proposed_destination.reason: The voice belongs to the brand; the neutral demo pack uses a library voice.

text: Whisper quirks: it writes numbers as digits, hallucinates repeated lines over digital silence at the end, and its word starts are off by tens of ms; normalise numbers before WER, ignore transcripts over silent tails, and snap starts to energy onsets.

proposed_destination.reason: Each quirk produced a false failure or a mistimed beat until handled.

text: VoiceProfile per brand: provider, voice id, model, format, cleanup chain, pace settings, lead and tail, and a lexicon of brand words and banned words for the Whisper checks.

proposed_destination.reason: Everything that made one film's voice work is data a second film can reuse.

text: TTS model picks (verified 2026-09-30): eleven_v4 is the most expressive (90+ languages, 10,000 characters a request); eleven_v4_turbo is the real-time, cheaper variant, not a better one; eleven_v3 and multilingual_v2 are previous generation.

proposed_destination.reason: Agents' training predates v4; the registry is where the current pick lives.

text: eleven_v4 follows inline audio tags and natural-language delivery direction more accurately than earlier models, and supports instant clones from 10 s of audio and professional clones.

proposed_destination.reason: Tags are worth using on v4 where they were unreliable before.

text: A/B eleven_v4 against multilingual_v2 for long reads (60-120 s narrations), which the vendor still calls its most stable long-form model.

proposed_destination.reason: A two-day-old model hadn't proven itself on long narration.

text: Always pass model_id: the Voice Design API defaults to the older ttv_v2 model and the Music API defaults to music_v1.

proposed_destination.reason: Vendor defaults lag their best models; an omitted id silently downgrades quality.

text: Voice Design parameters: a required description, preview text of 100-1,000 characters, loudness (-1 to 1, 0 is about -24 LUFS), seed, guidance scale (default 5), and reference audio and prompt strength on v3 only.

proposed_destination.reason: The design client validates these before spending a call.

text: Voice Design endpoints return 409 while a generation is in progress; run design calls one at a time per account.

proposed_destination.reason: Parallel design calls fail rather than queue.

text: Voice Design prompts follow the vendor's order (native language, gender and age range, quality, a 2-5 word persona, 2-3 emotion adjectives, then timbre, pacing and delivery); say 'thick' not 'strong' for accents, avoid 'reverb' or 'echo', and don't use 'accent' for intonation. Longer preview text is more stable, and higher guidance adheres more but risks quality.

proposed_destination.reason: Prompt wording decides the voice; the vendor's order is what its model was tuned on.

text: Stitch takes with previous_request_ids (up to 3) as well as previous and next text, fix a seed, and record the request id of every take.

proposed_destination.reason: Request-id stitching carries delivery across lines better than text alone, and ids make a re-voice match.

text: Whether eleven_v4 supports the with-timestamps endpoint isn't documented; verify before relying on TTS timestamps.

proposed_destination.reason: An undocumented behaviour can change without notice.

text: ElevenLabs Forced Alignment aligns audio to a known transcript (word and character timings; up to 3 GB, 10 hours and 675k characters; 29 languages; priced like speech-to-text; no diarized input).

proposed_destination.reason: The script is always known, which is exactly what alignment needs.

text: Evaluate Forced Alignment against Whisper on approved takes before switching; Whisper stays the default aligner meanwhile.

proposed_destination.reason: The inventory recommended replacing Whisper; the plan asks for evidence first.

text: Voice Isolator accepts up to 500 MB or an hour of audio or video and costs 1,000 characters per minute.
