proposed_destination.reason: It lowered a designed voice's floor only about 2 dB, so its cost rarely pays.

text: Text to Dialogue (for multi-voice pieces) recommends v4, keeps requests at or under 2,000 characters, has no speaker limit and now supports previous and next context.

proposed_destination.reason: The route for films with more than one voice.

text: ElevenLabs output from Beta Services can't be used commercially on any plan, and free-plan output can't be used commercially at all.

proposed_destination.reason: A beta feature in a published film is a licence breach.

text: A credit promotion on the new voice model that ends 2026-10-12.

proposed_destination.reason: Time-limited pricing; registry.json carries prices with verified-on dates.

text: eleven_v4 has no Style, Speed or SSML controls; only Stability and Similarity, and it accepts any stability value.

proposed_destination.reason: Settings that don't exist can't be tuned; pacing happens in post.

text: v4 audio tags come in families (emotion, delivery, long-narration direction, pacing, reactions, sound effects, accent).

proposed_destination.reason: Directors pick from a known vocabulary instead of inventing tags.

text: Tag rules: one tag per phrase; a tag at the head of a line carries the whole line; tags describe something audible and fit the voice's character; swap the tag rather than rewrite the text; never change the words.

proposed_destination.reason: Changed words break the script, captions and every word-anchored beat.

text: Designed voices perform worse on v4, so tags stay inside the designed character.

proposed_destination.reason: Pushing a designed voice outside its range exposes artifacts.

text: Tag failure modes to guard against: a tag spoken aloud, a tag performed as a sound effect, over-acting, drift between lines (record seed and request id), pauses that break the edit, and a take that no longer fits its shot.

proposed_destination.reason: Each has a check: Whisper, the fit check, recorded ids, or the owner's ear.

text: Voice gate: a tagged take's Whisper transcript contains no tag words and matches the script.

proposed_destination.reason: A tag read aloud is the most common v4 failure.

text: Tag A/B samples go through the exact approved cleanup and pacing chain, so the comparison hears the tags, not processing differences.

proposed_destination.reason: An unfair A/B picks the wrong version.

text: Audition clips for the owner are level-matched (both sides at -20 LUFS) and laid out A, a short gap, then B, with one reel of all pairs.

proposed_destination.reason: The louder side wins blind tests; matching removes the bias.

text: Voice gate: stripping the tags from the tagged script gives back the script exactly.

proposed_destination.reason: Tags must never smuggle in word changes.

text: One ElevenLabs client serves every voice and music tool (account, voice lookup, TTS with model, format, settings, seed and neighbour text), and one key resolver is shared by all of them.

proposed_destination.reason: Five tools imported one helper; one client keeps auth, retries and the ledger consistent.

text: Rebuild the mix automatically as builders' beats land, with a watcher that prints one PASS/FAIL line.

proposed_destination.reason: Builders export beats over hours; the watcher kept the sound current without anyone asking.

text: Picture events no longer carry synth sound parameters (the v1 approach); they carry a kind and a size, and sound is designed from them.

proposed_destination.reason: Superseded by the v2 beat vocabulary; Slate ships the v2 contract only.

text: The v1 cue sheets (a hand spotting sheet and one-recipe visual cues) are obsolete; later films carried empty stubs for them.

proposed_destination.reason: v2 families replaced them; shipping both pipelines confused tools and agents.

text: Default sound palette: pads, small soft felt notes, and hollow wood clicks and clacks; designed, not stock.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner's taste, proven on proof 2; it's the starting palette each brand's onboarding adapts.

text: No chimes, bells, metal, glass or buzzers in the effects.

proposed_destination.reason: Chimes were rejected on the first proof; a warning state is a falling wood pair, never a buzzer.

text: No room-tone drone: it read as 'a microwave'.

proposed_destination.reason: A continuous bed under the voice was rejected and removed from every film.

text: Never glide a sustained tone's pitch (it read as 'an air-raid siren'); move between notes by crossfading held notes, like a pad changing chord.

proposed_destination.reason: A hard rule in any renderer that sustains a pitch.

text: Keep any tonal bed about 20 LU under the voice and keep harmony out of the words (pads low-passed at or below 1.4 kHz under VO).

proposed_destination.reason: Voice first: the owner found the first mix 'a little bit too loud'.

text: The owner's taste is a default profile that each brand overrides in onboarding.

proposed_destination.reason: Every brand gets its own palette; the owner's is the starting point, never a hard-coded default.

text: Synthesized tonal layers sound cheap: compose the music (a score per act) and use real sampled instruments; keep synthesis for air, ink, beads and subs.

proposed_destination.reason: 'The tonal audio file is the problem… an entire rework and an entire rethink.'

text: Long one-shot music generations fail (a six-minute score had 21 s of silence over the reveal and 18 s of noise): compose one part per act, two takes each, QA every take and assemble on the story's landings; repair by holding a take's last chord instead of re-composing.

proposed_destination.reason: Per-act parts and measured assembly produced three clean scores; repairs by freeze cost no credits.

text: Music gate: no 0.5 s window of the music stem under -60 dBFS outside declared planned stops (each with a 'why'), predicted at assembly with the mix's gain law and measured again after the mix; takes open with their own silence (one bloom entered 0.75 s late).

proposed_destination.reason: Per-take QA misses short holes and late entries; this check catches them before the owner hears them.

text: Eleven Music's music_v2_5 rejected composition plans with sections cut to shots, so every score used music_v1; re-test the newest model with section plans before defaulting to it.

proposed_destination.reason: The best model on paper failed the pipeline's one hard requirement; the registry pin records what actually works.

text: Sound planner defaults: one family per interaction kind with designed variations, a round-robin that never repeats the last two, bursts treated as one gesture, at most one impact per act, and at most 8 short transients per 0.5 s.

proposed_destination.reason: One sound per loose kind produced 483 cues from 48 sounds with a run of 11; the planner rules brought it to 210 distinct sounds and a longest run of 1.

text: Repetition gate, measured from rendered cues: longest identical run 1, no runs of three or more, no sound serving two kinds, at most 3 identical sounds in any second ('same' means log-mel fingerprint distance under 3 dB).

proposed_destination.reason: 'The same tone a million times' was the complaint; a fingerprint count makes it measurable.

text: Every beat is tagged with a kind from a fixed vocabulary plus a size and a plain-language note; loose kinds ('click' meant a press, a check, a vertex and a row) made consistent sound impossible.

proposed_destination.reason: The beat vocabulary is the contract between picture builders and sound.

text: Sound sync gate: render each cue alone, find its perceptual anchor per family (strikes at the first sample within 12 dB of peak, paper within 30 dB, the pencil tip, the count settle, whoosh and swell crests, draw accents) and require it within one frame of its beat.

proposed_destination.reason: Sync is measured, not assumed: the worst anchors were 24.1 ms and 21.4 ms against a 33 ms frame.

text: Mix gate: integrated loudness -14 LUFS +-0.5 and true peak <= -1 dBTP (4x oversampled), measured with ebur128; the engine and version are recorded.

proposed_destination.reason: The web target every film met; broadcast and platform targets come from the format.

text: Mix format gate: 48 kHz / 24-bit, exactly the picture's length.

proposed_destination.reason: A mix a few microseconds short already cost frames at mux time.

text: Stems gate: dialogue, effects, ambience and music stems sum to the mix sample for sample (max abs difference about 1e-7).

proposed_destination.reason: Stems that don't sum make any later remix drift from the approved mix.

text: Mix defaults: music sits 15 LU under the voice with a 4 dB VO-keyed duck (80 ms attack, 650 ms release); the effects stem has a -7 dBTP ceiling; a transparent limiter works on the voice only.

proposed_destination.reason: Voice first, with every other stem capped relative to it.

text: Voice limiter gate: the voice-only limiter touches under 5% of the speech.

proposed_destination.reason: A limiter working harder than that is audible; the mix should rebalance instead.

text: Score take QA gate: flag silence (RMS under -45 dBFS) or noise (spectral flatness over 0.03, or a dull spectrum above -50 dBFS) lasting at least 1.5 s, ignoring the first and last second.

proposed_destination.reason: Eleven Music's two failure modes are silence and noise; every take gets checked before assembly.

text: Score assembly reads its landings (impacts, reveals, stops) from the film's timeline instead of a layout coded for one film.

proposed_destination.reason: One film's assembler hard-coded its act layout; the generic version reads landings.

text: The sound planner takes the character family, key and scale as configuration; the source films hard-coded one character's gesture mode and a D-major pentatonic.

proposed_destination.reason: Key, tempo and character motif are per brand and per film.

text: Ship one sound pipeline (the v2 family vocabulary); the v1 synth engine survives only for its eases, sampler, hall and mixer.

proposed_destination.reason: Two engines and two cue vocabularies coexisting confused tools and agents.

text: VO is levelled to about -20 dBFS RMS of its voiced part before the mix.

proposed_destination.reason: Levelling on voiced RMS keeps reads consistent whatever their pauses.

text: Score assembly places takes by measured entry, never plan time, and supports typed joins: film start, act crossfade, bloom on a landing, dead stop, drop to one held note, resume, thin to a still pad, lift onto an onset, and arrive with the last chord held to the final frame.

proposed_destination.reason: Typed joins let a score follow the story's landings without re-composing.

text: A sound proof video (a labelled log spectrogram with every cue marked by stem and timecode, plus a moving playhead) is a good review artefact for sound changes.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner reviews sound by ear; the spectrogram shows where each cue sits.

text: Build the sound bank from written recipes (seeded and deterministic) into per-family variation files plus a manifest and an audition file; ship the recipes, never the WAVs.

proposed_destination.reason: Recipes are portable and licence-clean; the rendered bank is neither.

text: The sound planner skips unreadable act files and reports them, and reports unknown beat kinds instead of silently dropping or guessing them.

proposed_destination.reason: Builders export beats over hours; one half-written file must not stop the mix or vanish from it.

text: The sound planner reads a per-family table (gain, pre-gain ceiling, duck depth, reverb send, gesture window, maximum rate, collision priority, pitch set); impacts never duck and swells duck deepest.

proposed_destination.reason: A brand retunes families without touching code.

text: Dedupe windows per family: the same family within 40 ms merges, counts within 0.45 s, swells within 2.5 s, impacts within 1 s, and whooshes within the larger of 0.35 s and 45% of the previous move.

proposed_destination.reason: Builders often export the same beat twice; doubled sounds read as mistakes.

text: Impacts are rationed to one per act at least 20 s apart; extras become large lands.

proposed_destination.reason: An impact means a big moment; more than one per act cheapens all of them.

text: A gesture (the same family within its window) thins to rate x span + 2 hits, keeping the first and last, with shaped levels (first full, inner 2.5-3.3 dB softer, last settling at -1 dB).

proposed_destination.reason: A list writing on is one gesture, not ten separate clicks.

text: A seeded shuffle bag per family and size plays every variant once per round, never the same twice in a row and never one of the last two at a new round; pitched families walk their pitch set (down when the beat's note says it falls) and turn back at the top.

proposed_destination.reason: Designed variation, not random noise, is what stopped 'the same tone a million times'.

text: Collisions within 35 ms: when both are tiny transients the lower-priority one drops, otherwise it's lowered 6 dB.

proposed_destination.reason: Two clicks on one frame read as a flam; priority keeps the meaningful one.

text: A 'held breath' note turns a swell, whoosh or draw into a rest: effects fall silent from there until the next impact, and designed silences are first-class cues with a reason.

proposed_destination.reason: Silence before a landing is designed, so the schema has to carry it.

text: Parametric sound cues follow the picture's data: typing strokes per beat with lead-ins, count ticks where the eased counter crosses steps (at least 45 ms apart, at most 14 a second) ending in a settle, draw sounds that follow pen speed and pan with the line, and whoosh peaks and swell crests on the beat.

proposed_destination.reason: Sounds generated from the picture's own motion stay in sync by construction.

text: Classify beats by their explicit kind, never by regex on builder ids or notes; regex rules (impact hints, legacy migration) were brittle and project-specific.

proposed_destination.reason: Words in ids change with every film; kinds are the contract.

text: Sound envelopes, filter sweeps and pans ride the same named eases as the picture.

proposed_destination.reason: A whoosh that follows the move's ease sounds attached to it.

text: One shared synthetic hall (2.4 s decorrelated noise, 20 ms predelay, 6.5 kHz low-pass) gives every effect the same space.

proposed_destination.reason: A single designed space keeps effects coherent across builders' acts.

text: Duck each stem under the voice by its own depth using a smoothed VO envelope; UI clicks never duck.

proposed_destination.reason: Ducked clicks would drift off their beat's perceived level; beds and effects need room for the voice.

text: A 25 Hz high-pass on the master removes subsonic energy before loudness normalization.

proposed_destination.reason: Subsonic energy wastes headroom and moves the loudness reading.

text: The mixer refuses with a non-zero exit ('needs a limiter') rather than hide a true-peak failure.

proposed_destination.reason: A mix that quietly fails its target is worse than one that stops.

text: When limiting is needed across stems, apply one linked gain curve to every stem (4x oversampled peaks, +-5 ms lookahead, 80 ms release) so the stems still sum to the mix; never use one-pass loudnorm for delivery.

proposed_destination.reason: Per-stem limiting or riding gain breaks the stem sum; a review mixer's stems couldn't sum for this reason.

text: Eleven Music calls can take minutes: use a long timeout (about 600 s) and pass output_format as a query parameter.

proposed_destination.reason: Default HTTP timeouts abort paid compositions midway.

text: Read-only scanners for installed sampler zone maps and Apple Loops metadata help find usable local instrument content on a new machine.

proposed_destination.reason: The bank builds from what's installed; knowing what's there comes first.

text: Loudness-match the bank per family and size: K-weighted loudest 50 ms for transients and 400 ms for long sounds, with size offsets (small -5 dB, large +3 dB) and a peak cap.

proposed_destination.reason: Families balanced at build time keep the planner's gains meaningful.

text: Retune recorded hits onto the score key by varispeed after measuring each one's fundamental (the strongest partial in its first 60 ms).

proposed_destination.reason: Real recordings keep their material and still sit in the key.

text: One family per kind of interaction, each its own material: wood for touch, paper for paper, graphite and ink for marks, air for moves, tuned air for chapter swells, a vessel timbre for a character and one deep landing for impacts.

proposed_destination.reason: 'Be strong-willed about what they are… keep everything consistent.'

text: Big impacts get a tempo echo on the score's BPM (a dotted eighth or a quarter), each repeat 6.5 dB softer and darker on the other side; a film never reuses an impact file.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner asked for a hero landing's impact to echo; it became the pattern for big moments.

text: A character can own a motif family (a signature timbre and a short motif) that no other effect family and no score uses.

proposed_destination.reason: A character's sound only reads as theirs if nothing else plays it.

text: The DSP helpers (filters, EQ, resonators, varispeed, BS.1770 loudness, timbre features, onsets) are generic and ship as they are.

proposed_destination.reason: Deterministic, dependency-light DSP is the reusable core of the sound work.

text: Designed silences mask the UI, effects and reverb sends with a 60 ms ramp.

proposed_destination.reason: A hard mute clicks; a short ramp reads as a held breath.

text: The effects engine ducks each family on a 60 ms attack / 450 ms release VO follower.

proposed_destination.reason: Faster than the music duck, so effects step aside for the words and come back between them.

text: Every placed cue is written to a render log (family, size, render, pan, gain, duck, stem, shot, events), which repetition checks read.

proposed_destination.reason: The log is the evidence for sync and repetition gates.

text: Voice placement gate: find every VO take in the dialogue stem by cross-correlation within +-50 ms; each must sit within 0.5 ms of its cue with correlation of about 0.99 or better.

proposed_destination.reason: Every take landed exactly (min correlation 0.990-0.999) on the three films; the gate keeps it that way.

text: 'Same sound' means a 40-band log-mel fingerprint of the first 1.5 s under a calibrated 3 dB distance (re-seeding moved it 0.02 dB, a 30% longer ring 5.5 dB, a semitone 11.3 dB); the fingerprint is blind past 1.5 s.

proposed_destination.reason: The repetition gate is only as good as its definition of 'same'.

text: Stem pitch scan: find onsets in a rendered stem and the note each rings at; one UI stem sat 71% on two notes, one of them off-key.

proposed_destination.reason: Pitch monotony and off-key clicks are audible but invisible in cue sheets.

text: For sound revisions, review a before/after of the same passage over the delivered picture, labelled, with a short card between.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner judges changes by ear in context, not from a mix in isolation.

text: Seam quality at score joins is measurable: level across the beat, the loudest window, the largest 100 ms step, dips, chroma cosine, centroid, log-mel distance and beat-phase error.

proposed_destination.reason: Two ways of making one swell were chosen by these numbers, not by argument.

text: Typical planned music stops: a silent opening second, a held breath before a hero moment, half a second before a reveal, and the ending.

proposed_destination.reason: Planned stops are declared with a 'why' so the gap check can tell them from holes.

text: Score plans carry the taste in their global styles: positives name instrumentation, mood, key, tempo, 'instrumental', 'sparse, leaves room for a narrator' and 'continuous, no silences or gaps'; negatives list the banned timbres.

proposed_destination.reason: Style words in the plan are how taste reaches the music model.

text: Each score landing records its source (a builder's impact beat, a Whisper word, a shot frame or an estimate).

proposed_destination.reason: Estimated landings are the first to check when a bloom misses.

text: The score never plays the effects' materials: plan negatives ban the effect families' instruments (woodblock, marimba, xylophone) and any timbre a character owns, plus vocals, choir, bells, chimes, glockenspiel, celesta, music box, vibraphone, crotales, drums, risers, sirens, pitch bends and white noise.

proposed_destination.reason: The first plans still allowed marimba and woodblock and the score collided with the effects.

text: Detect a take's real musical entry (the first 50 ms window within 12 dB of its median) and its last music (the last window within 20 dB), and place by those.

proposed_destination.reason: Takes fade in and out on their own schedule, whatever the plan said.

text: A bloom lands exactly on its landing with everything before it cut (25 ms fade); a dead stop cuts just before the moment with a 120 ms fade, using the take whose level is highest at the cut.

proposed_destination.reason: Blooms and stops are the score's sync points; they have to be frame-exact.

text: Choose takes by score QA first, then by fit (missing music, level at the stops).

proposed_destination.reason: A clean take that doesn't fit its landings still loses to one that does.

text: Shape per-act score loudness around -16 LUFS before the final mix.

proposed_destination.reason: Acts composed separately arrive at different levels.

text: End on the last frame: hold the final chord to the last frame and fade to silence on it, not before.

proposed_destination.reason: Music that stops before the picture ends reads as a mistake.

text: The composer runs a small worker pool with fixed seeds, retries with backoff, QA on every take and a credits record before and after each run.

proposed_destination.reason: Composition is the most expensive vendor call; it needs every safeguard.

text: Before assembly, check that each take reaches its hand-over, is still at level on its landings, and has a clear onset where it must lift (spectral-flux z above 8).

proposed_destination.reason: A take that fades before its hand-over leaves a hole the mix can't fix.

text: Eleven Music costs about 825 credits per minute of music; one brand film's score took about 26,000 credits across 32 takes, another about 9,200.

proposed_destination.reason: Scores dominate a film's ElevenLabs spend; budgets come from these numbers.

text: A generated plate's native audio can serve as ambience: high-pass it at 60 Hz and sit it about 30 LU under the voice; generating with sound cost about 1.5x silent on one model.

proposed_destination.reason: Matched ambience under a plate is nearly free when it comes with the generation.

text: Apple's GarageBand, Logic and Final Cut sound content may be used inside finished productions but not redistributed as samples; a bank of single hits built from it is sample-like, so Slate builds the bank locally from each machine's installed content.

proposed_destination.reason: Shipping the rendered bank in a public package would breach the content licence.

text: A fully synthetic or CC0 fallback bank for hosts without Apple sound content.

proposed_destination.reason: Superseded by the plan: tonal roles need real sampled instruments, so doctor fails and names what to install; synthesis stays only for air, ink, beads and subs.

text: Timbre gate: each family's median spectral centroid at or below 1.5 kHz, no high partials outliving a strike (no chime tails), nothing metallic or glassy, and pitched families on the score key's pentatonic; the films recorded these features but never failed a build on them.

proposed_destination.reason: The v1 redesign moved the effects centroid from 583 to 382 Hz and energy above 2 kHz from 3.7% to 1.2%; the gate keeps new families in that range.

text: Anchor multi-note gestures on each note, not the summed gesture: one character gesture failed sync by 107.7 ms, likely because the verifier found the first note's onset on the summed gesture whose peak sat well above the soft first note.

proposed_destination.reason: A measurement artifact that fails a correct mix erodes trust in every gate.

text: Silence is a tool: hold a breath before a landing (effects fall silent, the music stops dead), open out of silence, and end on the last frame.

proposed_destination.reason: The biggest moments in the films landed out of silence.

text: Score in one key and put every pitched effect on that key's pentatonic, never on a leading tone, so nothing clashes.

proposed_destination.target: src/slate/sound/ (pitch sets from the score key)
proposed_destination.reason: Off-key UI clicks under a composed score were the most audible v1 flaw.

text: Restraint: only what the eye follows makes a sound.

proposed_destination.reason: Sound for every visible change turns a film into noise.

text: Eleven Music ignores plan edges (every take fades in over 0.5-3 s and out over 2-4 s): give every plan a 3 s pre-roll section cut at assembly, and run parts at least 3 s past any hand-over (4.5 s past a dead stop).

proposed_destination.reason: Without pre-rolls and overruns, every join starts in a fade.

text: Plan gate: split any part longer than about 90 s at a story turn; long plans ran out of material 7-18 s early.

proposed_destination.reason: An act went silent before its end because the part was too long.

text: Plan gate: every section lasts at least 3 s (duration_ms >= 3000).

proposed_destination.reason: The music API rejects shorter sections.

text: A moment that must land exactly is a part boundary on word times, never a section inside a take.

proposed_destination.reason: Sections inside a take don't land where the plan says; part boundaries can be placed exactly.

text: Eleven Music often won't deliver a requested dynamic (a requested swell rose 1.1 dB; four retries never lifted and cost 1,204 credits): measure every take at its landing, choose or splice from takes on hand before re-composing, and keep every take.

proposed_destination.reason: The swell that worked was an unused crescendo from another part.

text: Close holes in place with a phase-vocoder freeze of the previous part's last chord and an equal-power handover over 0.8 s; moving parts to close a hole cascaded into the next seams.

proposed_destination.reason: A freeze repair costs no credits and touches only the hole.

text: Crossfade with true equal-power (sin/cos amplitude) gains; squared gains dipped 3 dB between two different takes.

proposed_destination.reason: Uncorrelated takes need amplitude equal power, not power-squared gains.

text: Measure level changes in stereo: a mono fold faked a 3.8 dB rise through channel correlation that measured 0.0 dB in stereo.

proposed_destination.reason: A wrong measurement picked the wrong take once.

text: Effects creep above the voice unless capped: use family ceilings, stem trims and a -7 dBTP effects ceiling in the mix, and calibrate a redesign to the last approved level (within 1 LU) so an A/B hears design, not volume.

proposed_destination.reason: 'A little bit too loud' was the owner's first note on the effects.

text: Anchor sounds by what the ear hears: impose designed envelopes so crests land on the beat (a pencil tick led its letter by 80-210 ms; noisy crests put whoosh and swell peaks 75-920 ms off), place by perceptual onset and verify per family.

proposed_destination.reason: File start is not when a sound is heard.

text: Compensate limiter lookahead: ffmpeg alimiter without latency=1 lands the voice 240 samples late.

proposed_destination.reason: A 5 ms voice offset is enough to fail placement and blur consonants.

text: Everything is deterministic: seeds live in config, the same beats give the same cues, and plan files are immutable once composed (regenerating one plan never rewrites another's record).

proposed_destination.reason: Determinism is what makes a rebuild match the delivered film.

text: Score QA thresholds (flatness, peakiness) were tuned on one vendor's takes; re-check them when the music model changes.

proposed_destination.reason: Heuristics tuned on one model produce false passes or failures on the next.

text: The sound skill carries the taste rules, the Eleven Music playbook and the licensing notes; the voice skill carries the voice-brief template.

proposed_destination.reason: Knowledge that only lived in project docs becomes skill references.

text: Eleven Music parameters: a prompt or a composition plan, music_length_ms from 3,000 to 600,000 (the capability page says 5 minutes; verify per model), model_id, force_instrumental, a seed, respect_sections_durations (enforced from v2), inpainting and C2PA signing, with output_format as a query parameter.

proposed_destination.reason: Conflicting docs mean the limits get checked live, not assumed.

text: Eleven Music seeds don't guarantee exact reproducibility; keep every take and lock approved ones as assets.

proposed_destination.reason: A 're-run with the same seed' may not give back the approved score.

text: Eleven Music's self-serve plans exclude film, TV, radio and studio games (Enterprise needed); streaming rights start at Creator; reseller and music-library use are excluded; free output needs attribution. Broadcast formats flag the music terms.

proposed_destination.reason: A score is in most films; its terms decide where a film can air.

text: Music prompts never contain artist, songwriter, song or label names or substantial lyrics, and never ask to mimic an artist; outputs aren't exclusive, and some industries are excluded.

proposed_destination.reason: The music terms forbid it; the plan generator enforces it.

text: ElevenLabs Sound Effects: one model, 0.5-30 s, prompt influence 0.3 by default, optional loop, output as mp3, PCM up to 48 kHz or opus (no WAV container, so wrap PCM locally), about 40 credits a second.

proposed_destination.reason: Vendor SFX only fills a named gap; these are its limits when it does.

text: Generating the whole effects palette once with the vendor's SFX model and storing it as WAV.

proposed_destination.reason: The plan keeps a designed palette built locally from recipes and sampled instruments; vendor SFX only fills a named gap.

text: HyperFrames' voice-over 'carve' (band-limited ducking) with effect chains and submix buses is prior art for Slate's mix.

proposed_destination.reason: Band-limited ducking keeps music fuller than a broadband duck.

text: Character sound attacks sit on contact frames, one sound per frame with a priority order.

proposed_destination.reason: Two attacks on one frame blur the gesture's sound.

text: Sound markers are a schema of their own (film in and out, sample rate, markers with time, shot, type, stem and note), read by validation and repetition checks.

proposed_destination.reason: QA reads markers instead of re-deriving cue positions.

text: VO cues fade in over 10 ms and out over 50 ms.

proposed_destination.reason: Short fades remove clicks without eating consonants.

text: Sounds synthesized by Slate's own code (modal wood, beads, ink, air, tuned-air swells, subs) are Slate's to redistribute; only sampled Apple content is restricted.

proposed_destination.reason: Knowing which sounds are free to ship shapes the neutral demo pack.

text: Price the model shortlist with the vendor's estimate endpoint before generating anything.

proposed_destination.reason: The estimate call is free and catches surprises; Slate records it in the ledger before any spend.

text: Keep rejected and superseded generations with review sheets and provenance instead of deleting them.

proposed_destination.reason: Rejected takes explain later decisions and sometimes get reused (as a matte, for example).

text: Conform generated plates to the film: ProRes 422 HQ at native fps, motion-compensated interpolation to the film rate, a JPEG image sequence, and the plate's native audio as a 48 kHz/24-bit ambience file.

proposed_destination.reason: The films did the rate conform and image-sequence export by hand; Slate scripts the whole chain.

text: Every generation gets a manifest row: model, prompt, request id, job, dimensions, fps, provenance, licence and cost.

proposed_destination.reason: Provenance and cost per generation are what the ledger, the delivery manifest and later audits need.

text: Inspect interpolation on every shot that uses a conformed plate.

proposed_destination.reason: Motion-compensated interpolation can smear or tear; nobody else will look for it.

text: Asset ledger template: picture-from-code sources, every generation (model, request, output, status, cost), look and bridge tests, voice and music usage, sound sources and spend by balance.

proposed_destination.reason: Provenance and licence per asset are what a published film needs.

text: No generation without the brand kit's references attached and its tokens spelled into the prompt; ungrounded moodboards drifted into generic grey glass.

proposed_destination.reason: Grounding is the difference between on-brand and generic output.

text: Give generators a full reference pack (brand, UI frames, reference-film frames, first and last frames) wherever uploads are allowed; text-only prompts starved them.

proposed_destination.reason: 'Were we just flying blind?': once references were uploaded, fidelity improved.

text: Never put generated motion on screen where code or real footage exists; use a generation for shape, timing or texture (for example as a matte over real frames), judge at least two takes and check joins numerically. Background-only first and last frames made a model draw its own guide line 60-100 px off.

proposed_destination.reason: Generated pixels on screen read as AI and were rejected; the generation's shape used as a matte was approved.

text: Generated plates are atmosphere only: never UI, text, charts or logos; only the film's line and type go over them, with no extra blur.

proposed_destination.reason: Generated UI or text would be invented product; atmosphere is where generation earns its place.

text: Video models differ in brief fidelity: one family came out painterly and off-palette, another broke the brief with an extra element, a third matched the keyframes; keep a model routing table and a plate review sheet.

proposed_destination.reason: Model choice per shot type matters as much as the prompt.

text: Generate through the Cloud API (the one funded lane) and re-check the live catalog before assuming a capability gap; use other routes only for real gaps (the Cloud API had no voice models, so voice went to ElevenLabs direct).

proposed_destination.reason: Catalogs change weekly; a stale assumption sends work down the wrong billing lane.

text: The AI-bridge matte runs as a function with its timings and paths as parameters; the source tool hard-coded one shot.

proposed_destination.reason: The technique is the approved answer to 'AI pixels read as AI'; it has to work for any shot.

text: Never retry a POST to a paid generation API: a retried submit bills twice; recover by polling the request id instead.

proposed_destination.reason: Duplicate billing on a flaky network is the default failure of naive retry loops.

text: Cancelling a waiting generation (Ctrl-C or slate job cancel) cancels the remote request too.

proposed_destination.reason: A local cancel that leaves the remote job running still spends credits.

text: Plate feature tracking (a ridgeline every 0.25 s as 64 points with temporal median smoothing) takes its colour mask as configuration; the source was tuned to one palette.

proposed_destination.reason: Tracking a plate's shape is reusable for any brand once the mask isn't hard-coded.

text: Feature trackers hop between near-equal features, and edge tracking is valid only inside the intersection window: follow the feature, hold outside the reliable window and apply a temporal median.

proposed_destination.reason: A summit hop and fog pulling a track 200 px off both came from trusting every frame.

text: The hosted generation connector's AE recipes are free text, but generating inside them spends the separate app-credit pool, not the Cloud API balance.

proposed_destination.reason: The app-credit pool isn't funded; a recipe that generates would silently fail or spend the wrong money.

text: Plate briefs are templates, and every brand keeps its own reference pack for generations.

proposed_destination.reason: A plate brief plus the brand's references is what grounds a generation.

text: The ElevenLabs connector also exposes third-party image and video models (Veo, Seedance, Runway, GPT Image, Nano Banana, FLUX) and lipsync; generations there bill ElevenLabs credits and bypass Slate's ledger.

proposed_destination.reason: Chat-side generations have to be reconciled by balance snapshots.

text: The generation vendor's catalogue spans video, image, audio (including resold ElevenLabs voices) and 3D models; check it live before assuming a gap.

proposed_destination.reason: The catalogue changes weekly.

text: The generation vendor's CLI bills the app-credit pool (separate from the Cloud API), estimates with 'generate cost' and signs in by browser OAuth; Slate generates only through the Cloud API.

proposed_destination.reason: Only the Cloud API balance is funded.

text: The Cloud API bills per successful generation with no subscription, authenticates with 'Authorization: Key id:secret' and starts at 20 concurrent requests per key.

proposed_destination.reason: The client and the per-service lock use these limits.

text: Handle every generation status (queued, in progress, completed, failed, NSFW, cancelled), not just completed and failed; the Python SDK takes HF_KEY or a key and secret pair, and the JS SDK's v1 is deprecated.

proposed_destination.reason: An NSFW rejection that looks like a hang wastes a job slot.

text: The Cloud API's dollar-for-dollar cashback (the original reason for 'API first').

proposed_destination.reason: It ended 2026-09-30 23:59 UTC; the Cloud API stays the one lane by the owner's decision, not the promotion.

text: The Cloud API (with webhooks, 20 concurrent requests per key to start) is Slate's one generation lane; the vendor's CLI and skills stay available for direct use on app credits, and the hosted connector serves chat.

proposed_destination.reason: One funded lane keeps spend in one ledger.

text: The generation vendor's estimate endpoint can answer 409 'temporarily unavailable'; retry the estimate, never skip it.

proposed_destination.reason: Skipping a failed estimate is how unbudgeted spend happens.

text: Generated plates use the best available model by default (the owner asked for 'the highest-level API model'), overridable per film.

proposed_destination.reason: Best quality wins; the registry names the current best model.

text: The generation vendor keeps outputs for about 7 days: download every result immediately and record its local path in the manifest.

proposed_destination.reason: A result left on the vendor's side disappears with its cost already paid.

text: Generation prices seen on the films (list, September 2026): about $1.14 a second for 1080p image-to-video on the best video model, $0.68 a second for video extension, $0.76-0.91 a clip on another model, and about $4.55 per bridge take; a whole film generated at 1080p would cost about $400-600.

proposed_destination.reason: Real prices anchor estimates and default budgets.

text: A 4K upscale through the voice vendor's connector costs about 6,800 credits per 8 seconds, so upscaling a whole film (about 310k credits) exceeds a Creator plan; upscales are per-shot decisions with an estimate.

proposed_destination.reason: An innocent 'upscale the film' would spend two months of credits.

text: video-verifier's Simulator recording script is the starting point for iOS captures; its Playwright web path is never used, because web captures go through Aside.

proposed_destination.reason: The capture module reuses what works and removes the second browser.

text: iOS captures use xcrun simctl from Xcode's command-line tools, which the owner installs.

proposed_destination.reason: Doctor checks for them only when a film needs an iOS capture.

text: An agent without a video pipeline hand-built silent reels from Simulator captures with PIL and an ffmpeg binary borrowed from another app's bundle; Slate's capture path and a doctor-installed ffmpeg replace that.

proposed_destination.reason: Silent, unchecked reels are the gap Slate fills for autonomous agents.

text: Builders make only stills and half-scale previews (no motion-blur samples) in scratch space, never full-resolution finals and never inside the project folder.

proposed_destination.reason: Finals are central and queued; builder previews in the project folder polluted it and loaded the machine.

text: Final renders average 16 motion-blur sub-frames across a 180-degree shutter in 16-bit and write ProRes 422 HQ 10-bit per act.

proposed_destination.reason: True motion blur without colour shifts; the renderer is the heart of the engine.

text: Register every act render with its composition, shots, file, film frame_in and exclusive frame_out, and a history of every partial re-render and splice.

proposed_destination.reason: Every later tool (AE build, QA, review cuts, validation) reads the registry; its history is the provenance.

text: Remotion's CameraMotionBlur is 8-bit additive and shifts flat colours; render sub-frames and average them in 16-bit instead.

proposed_destination.reason: Colour shifts on flat brand colours are exactly what a paper look can't hide.

text: Video decoders crash long parallel renders: play plates as JPEG sequences from film time, with frame = round((t - t0) x fps) shared by every motion-blur sub-sample.

proposed_destination.reason: An OffthreadVideo EPIPE crashed a final render; image sequences never did.

text: Prove every partial re-render before replacing the act: stream-copy splice (ProRes is intra-only), unchanged frame count, matching hashes at FROM-1 and TO+1, and a PSNR edge scan over +-2 frames that rejects a better match at another offset.

proposed_destination.reason: Splicing saves hours, but only proven splices are safe; a misnumbered patch looks fine in a still.

text: A second render machine was about 5x faster, but rendering is now local by default; a remote backend is optional, with lossless transport, a private toolchain, quiet/unquiet hooks and a local fallback when it drops off the network.

proposed_destination.reason: One film had to render locally when the remote machine dropped; the owner has since ruled local rendering the default.

text: Keep heavy outputs out of cloud-synced folders: iCloud used about 1.5 cores and evicted files on a 94%-full disk; films live outside iCloud and heavy folders carry .nosync names.

proposed_destination.reason: Sync churn slowed renders and evicted inputs mid-build.

text: KeepAlive services restart when killed: boot them out, wait until they're really gone, record their state, and restore exactly in reverse with retries.

proposed_destination.reason: A hasty restore once lost a service; the pattern generalizes to any 'quiet the machine' hook.

text: Machine-specific setup from the films: a company laptop's repo, its render mirror and services, and the project's knowledge-base paths.

proposed_destination.reason: Company machines are never used for renders now, and machine paths never belong in a shareable core.

text: The source films' remote render script (a specific host, company services in its quiet list, a private npm path, a mirror that skipped one film's data).

proposed_destination.reason: Rendering on that machine is retired; the pattern survives only as an optional generic remote backend.

text: Sub-frame sampling: with S samples per frame, sample k of frame f sits at f - 0.25 + 0.5 x (k + 0.5)/S (a 180-degree shutter at -90-degree phase, centred on the frame), and film time is (first shot's frame_in + local frame)/fps.

proposed_destination.reason: The formula is the contract between the kit clock and the motion-blur renderer.

text: Each act composition's frame 0 is its first shot's film frame, and its registered duration is the span's frames times the motion-blur sub-sample count.

proposed_destination.reason: Registering acts this way lets the renderer ask for any sub-sampled range directly.

text: Remotion renders with GL through ANGLE (Metal on the Mac), lossless PNG frames and overwrite on.

proposed_destination.reason: PNG frames keep the motion-blur average lossless; ANGLE is the GPU path that worked.

text: Render many stills from one bundle (composition, frames, scale, props) instead of bundling per still.

proposed_destination.reason: Each bundle is about 290 MB and takes time; one bundle per film per source hash is the rule.

text: The motion-blur renderer bundles once, renders every sub-frame as a PNG buffer in order and streams them to ffmpeg (rgb48 tmix over the samples, select every S-th, yuv422p10le, ProRes 422 HQ with BT.709 tags) with no intermediates on disk.

proposed_destination.reason: Streaming keeps disk use flat and the 16-bit average exact.

text: For remote transport, write lossless x264 10-bit 4:2:2 .mkv (8-13x smaller than ProRes on paper and UI frames, bit-exact) and encode ProRes locally on arrival.

proposed_destination.reason: A relayed network link ran at 0.5-19 MB/s; ProRes would not have fit.

text: Every render and still script deletes its temp bundle (about 290 MB) on exit; 56 leaked bundles once filled 14 GB, and the stills script still leaked.

proposed_destination.reason: Disk filled silently during production; cleanup on exit is mandatory, including on failure.

text: A remote render mirror must sync code and data together, atomically; a mirror with new word timings and old act code couldn't bundle.

proposed_destination.reason: Half-synced mirrors fail in confusing ways far from the change that caused them.

text: Local renders run at low concurrency (2) while builders are working.

proposed_destination.reason: The machine is shared with builders' previews and checks.

text: Motion-blur defaults: a 180-degree shutter at -90-degree phase with 16 samples; 32 samples on portal zooms; a 270-360-degree shutter only on a carrier's fastest 6 frames; never add blur to generated footage (its blur is baked in).

proposed_destination.reason: More samples only where the motion needs them keeps render time sane.

text: Chrome's 3D sorting races with many parallel planes (a card face dropped for 2 frames) and raster tiles go missing under heavy load: keep few parallel planes, one explicit stacking order with each layer its own context, moderate render concurrency, and glitch-scan every render.

proposed_destination.reason: These one-frame drops only appear in final renders under load, so every render gets scanned.

text: Every ProRes Slate writes carries BT.709 primaries, transfer and matrix tags (prores_ks profile 3, vendor apl0, yuv422p10le), and blur averaging happens in 16-bit RGB before the 10-bit conversion.

proposed_destination.reason: Untagged footage is what made AE guess its colour space.

text: A remote render machine receives only the film project and returns only finished renders; nothing from a company repo travels either way.

proposed_destination.reason: Company code never leaves its machine; render mirrors must not become a path out.

text: The remote backend's quiet hooks are a user-supplied list; no service names are baked into Slate.

proposed_destination.reason: The films' list named one company's services.

text: Offer the File Provider ignore attribute for film folders that must live under iCloud Drive, alongside .nosync names for heavy folders.

proposed_destination.reason: Some owners keep projects in iCloud; the attribute keeps sync off the heavy media.

text: A Remotion licence key, when configured, is passed to renderMedia and renderStill through @remotion/licensing (4.0.237+), which sends usage events only, never content.

proposed_destination.reason: Company use may need the key; the renderer should accept it without code changes.

text: Remotion's HtmlInCanvasMotionBlur (4.0.529+, 8 samples by default, 180-degree shutter, no nesting, preview behind a Chrome flag) is worth testing against Slate's sub-frame renderer, which stays the default.

proposed_destination.reason: The inventory recommended it as the default; the plan keeps the proven renderer until a test says otherwise.

text: Tune render concurrency per machine with npx remotion benchmark instead of the default (half the CPU threads), which can overload the machine and crash renders.

proposed_destination.reason: A load average of 293 on 14 cores showed what untuned concurrency does.

text: Remotion performance notes: prefer @remotion/media's Video over OffthreadVideo, precompute GPU-heavy CSS (blur, shadows, gradients) on GPU-less machines, and use PNG frames only where alpha or lossless averaging needs them.

proposed_destination.reason: Builders choose techniques; these are the costly ones.

text: Remotion ProRes: profiles run proxy to 4444-xq (hq by default); alpha needs 4444 plus PNG frames and yuva444p10le; crf is unsupported and videoBitrate ignored.

proposed_destination.reason: Alpha deliverables need a different pixel path.

text: Remotion's distributed renders need equal chunk frame ranges (except the last), identical options, h264-ts chunks, an enforced audio track, compositionStart and seamless AAC (or PCM) audio, merged with combineChunks().

proposed_destination.reason: Chunking by hand without these rules produces audio pops and off-by-one joins.

text: HyperFrames (Apache-2.0: HTML and seekable animation to deterministic MP4) is prior art for the open web renderer; its router skill, frozen-file asset ledger and non-interactive skill updates are patterns to learn from.

proposed_destination.reason: Learn from it (Apache-2.0 allows it); Slate's web renderer shares the film clock with the other engines.

text: claude-motion-design (HTML plus Playwright plus ffmpeg, no Remotion licence) is prior art for a Remotion-free renderer; Slate's version captures only its own local pages with puppeteer and never browses.

proposed_destination.reason: The web renderer must not become a second browser.

text: A render replaces the registered file only when its frame count matches the registry span; otherwise the old render stays and the job reports failure.

proposed_destination.reason: A short render silently replacing a good one would corrupt the film.

text: After every act render, stamp its registry entry and run the glitch scan, writing the flags beside the render.

proposed_destination.reason: Evidence produced at render time is never skipped later.

text: Renders run at a lower CPU priority so the machine stays usable for everything else.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner works on the same Mac while films render.

text: Generate the render registry from shots.json (one entry per act with its span), keep an entry's history only when its range and file are unchanged, and assert acts cover 0 to the film's total frames; two films kept theirs by hand.

proposed_destination.reason: Every downstream tool reads the registry; a hand-kept one drifts.

text: The fast-variant editor refuses tracks with a single key (it needs two or more), zero-width masks, and GLSL that paints outside its raster box.

proposed_destination.reason: These refusals only surface at render time.

text: In the fast-variant editor, motion blur on frames whose children have shadows makes hard, fringed halos; skip blur on shadow-bearing frames.

proposed_destination.reason: The halos look like a compositing bug.

text: The fast-variant editor rasterizes a node's mask at canvas size from the node's own origin (feathering softens that raster's edges), and mask width grows from the mask's centre.

proposed_destination.reason: Masks placed with browser assumptions land in the wrong place.

text: The fast-variant editor's presigned upload slots expire in under an hour, despite a stated 24 hours; upload right before use.

proposed_destination.reason: An upload prepared early fails at render time.

text: The fast-variant editor's 16-sample motion-blur cap shows steps on whips; ramp the blur instead.

proposed_destination.reason: Stepped blur on a whip reads as a frame drop.

text: The fast-variant editor's sandbox runs cost no credits and render about 67 ms a frame at 1080p, but a 100 s render took 94-577 s end to end.

proposed_destination.reason: Cost is nil but wall-clock time varies sixfold.

text: The fast-variant editor's workflow docs live only behind the vendor's connector; record the version used with each variant.

proposed_destination.reason: Undocumented, fast-moving tools need their version pinned in the film's record.

text: The toolchain proof is a scripted After Effects smoke test: build a 1-second comp with one eased shape, render it with aerender, require exactly 30 frames, and measure the ease in pixels (within 1.5 px from frame 6 on; the first motion-blurred frame measured 4.2 px).

proposed_destination.reason: Proves AE, aerender, scripting and ease conversion end to end before any film depends on them.

text: After Effects' 'Allow Scripts to Write Files and Access Network' is a security control only the owner switches; the finishing route works with it off by reporting through AE's preferences file.

proposed_destination.reason: Slate never changes this pref, and its prefs tool refuses the key; building scenes through the bridge is the only thing that needs it.

text: The AE project is built from data: one comp per shot holding its slice of the act render, one comp per act, and a master comp with the final mix and markers for every shot, spoken word and event.

proposed_destination.reason: An editable AE project that mirrors the film's data is the finish the owner can open and adjust.

text: Before any rebuild, save whatever AE project is open (to a preserved folder) and never discard user work; probes run only in an empty untitled project and clean up after themselves.

proposed_destination.reason: The driver must never cost the owner an unsaved edit.

text: Set the AE working space to the profile AE assigns to the incoming footage (BT.709-tagged renders -> Rec.709 Gamma 2.4) so AE converts nothing; an sRGB working space darkened a deep brand colour by about 8 code values (33 dB). Footage profiles and output colour aren't scriptable in AE 26.5, so the working space is the only lever.

proposed_destination.reason: Colour conversion is silent in AE; only a PSNR check against the renders found it.

text: Start every nested layer 0.1 frame early: placed exactly on k x 1001/30000 s, AE showed the previous frame from one act on (picture 33 ms behind sound), and AE's own +-0.5-frame tolerance couldn't see it; check placement at 0.02 frame.

proposed_destination.reason: Sub-frame placement errors cause duplicated and dropped frames at cuts.

text: AE's stock 'High Quality' output module is ProRes 422 (apcn), not 422 HQ, and output-module codecs can't be set by script: render the stock 'High Quality with Alpha' (4444) and conform to 422 HQ with ffmpeg prores_ks profile 3.

proposed_destination.reason: Trusting the template name would have delivered the wrong codec.

text: One long aerender grows until the Mac swaps and aborts: render masters in chunks (8 for a six-minute film), a fresh aerender per chunk with -mem_usage 25 50, up to three tries, resume by frame count, and the AE GUI quit first.

proposed_destination.reason: Chunked fresh processes finished where one long render failed.

text: AE's disk cache filled 60 GB during one master: turn it off for masters (with AE closed) and restore the owner's setting afterwards, with a watchdog that stops the render under 4 GB free; masters peaked around 20 GB of disk.

proposed_destination.reason: The disk filled mid-master on a 99%-full machine; the watchdog exists because of it.

text: ffprobe prints AE QuickTime streams twice (a stream group); a shared frame-count helper takes the first integer.

proposed_destination.reason: Whole-string frame-count comparisons failed on AE output.

text: AE 26.5's AppleScript DoScript and DoScriptFile return 0 for every call, so scripts report through app.settings plus saveToDisk and a reader parses AE's prefs file; switch to JSON report files only when the file-write pref is on, keeping the settings channel as the fallback.

proposed_destination.reason: Without a side channel the driver can't tell success from failure.

text: AE project audit gate: 16 bpc, the working space matching the footage, linear blending off, shot comps matching shots.json to the frame (size, pixel aspect, fps, slice start within 0.02 frame), no placeholders or missing footage, act order, master frames, audio covering the film and markers, no missing or substituted fonts, no expression errors, and native motion blur on animated layers.

proposed_destination.reason: Fourteen checks passed on the re-delivered film; unchecked items report UNCHECKED, never pass.

text: The ES3 library takes comp names, the act list and the film id as parameters instead of per-film wrapper scripts.

proposed_destination.reason: One wrapper file per film (and no support for a third) doesn't scale.

text: The AE master path depends on stock output-module template names and on toggling AE's disk-cache preference in a prefs file with AE closed, which is fragile across AE versions; doctor checks the templates exist and the prefs tool edits byte-safely.

proposed_destination.reason: A renamed template or a mangled prefs file would break masters silently.

text: SVG-to-AE shape conversion supports only M/L/H/V/C/Z path commands with translate and scale transforms; logos with arcs or other transforms must be flattened first.

proposed_destination.reason: Native AE logo builds fail quietly on unsupported path commands.

text: AE cold-starts in about 41 s (about 1 s warm); the driver uses a 600 s AppleEvent timeout and takes the AE app name from config.

proposed_destination.reason: A short timeout fails the first call of every session.

text: Each host app that drives AE needs macOS Automation permission; the first call prompts and a denial shows as osascript error -1743, so doctor checks it from each real context (Claude Code, a Codex slice, the OpenClaw gateway).

proposed_destination.reason: A permission granted to one terminal doesn't cover another agent's process.

text: One cross-process lock covers every route into AE (osascript scripts, the AE bridge, aerender): AE shows a blocking modal when a second script arrives mid-run, and a file write with the pref off can raise a modal that stalls the call.

proposed_destination.reason: A modal freezes AE until a person clicks OK; two agents on one AE is the easiest way to get one.

text: ExtendScript is ES3: var only, no JSON object, indexOf, forEach, map, trim or Object.keys, no trailing commas, each script an IIFE returning a string, properties addressed by match name, ease arrays sized to the property (1 for spatial, 3 for scale), and eases read back after they're set.

proposed_destination.reason: Modern JavaScript in an AE script fails at run time, far from the author.

text: Parse JSON inside AE with a vetted json2.jsx, not eval (eval is tolerable only for Slate's own generated JSON).

proposed_destination.reason: eval on untrusted JSON is code execution inside AE.

text: Set Mercury Software Only on footage-only AE projects: aerender crashed twice in the GPU compositor under memory pressure.

proposed_destination.reason: Masters of pre-rendered footage gain nothing from the GPU and lose stability.

text: The AE bridge exchanges request and response files through a per-user mailbox and keeps its own busy lock (stale after 90 s); Slate's AE lock shares that lock so neither side runs a script while the other does.

proposed_destination.reason: Two independent locks on one AE are no lock at all.

text: Every bridge call runs inside one undo group, with default timeouts of 60 s (120 s to render a frame, 10 minutes to import).

proposed_destination.reason: Long imports and renders need their own timeouts or they read as failures.

text: Doctor reports the AE bridge connected only after a live ae_project_info call succeeds; the bridge's own doctor checks files only.

proposed_destination.reason: A bridge that installs cleanly still can't complete a call without the file-write pref.

text: Keep the bridge's arbitrary eval off, restrict its categories when a job needs only a few, and treat its mailbox folder as a code-execution trust boundary (write access to it runs code in AE).

proposed_destination.reason: The bridge is a remote-control channel into AE; its defaults should stay tight.

text: The bridge's frame render handles colour-managed projects with a transient display-transform layer and warns when it falls back; its frames aren't colour evidence unless that warning is clear.

proposed_destination.reason: A preview frame with the wrong transform would mislead a colour check.

text: Neither ExtendScript nor the bridge can pick the codec inside an output module's format options.

proposed_destination.reason: Codec choice has to come from stock templates plus an ffmpeg conform.

text: A queued render is not proof: check the output file exists with the expected template, bitrate and frame count.

proposed_destination.reason: The bridge's own validation guide says so, and the films hit the template trap.

text: saveFrameToPng can silently drop files; verify every expected frame file exists after a frame export.

proposed_destination.reason: A missing frame looks like success until something reads it.

text: A timeout leaves an AE mutation's state unknown, and bridge batches aren't transactional: inspect the project before retrying any mutation.

proposed_destination.reason: Blind retries double-apply half-finished edits.

text: Find AE's prefs folder by version sort, not text sort ('26.10' sorts before '26.5' as text).

proposed_destination.reason: The report reader would silently read an old version's prefs after an update.

text: Find AE and aerender by discovery (app bundle lookup), not a hard-coded, year-versioned path.

proposed_destination.reason: The next AE release changes the folder name.

text: The master chunk count lives in one config value shared by the render-queue script and the masters runner; the films kept two copies that had to match by hand.

proposed_destination.reason: Mismatched counts render the wrong spans.

text: Import vector logos into AE as editable shapes via PDF and 'Create Shapes from Vector Layer', looking the menu command up by name (its numeric id varies), in an empty project that's cleaned up afterwards.

proposed_destination.reason: Editable shapes are what native AE logo builds need.

text: A generated clip was imported into an AE comp, titled on a brand ease, saved and rendered by aerender end to end during the toolchain proof.

proposed_destination.reason: It proves generated footage and AE finishing work together.

text: A capability probe (colour API keys, TextDocument properties, output-module and render-settings templates, required effects by match name) runs in an empty project as part of doctor.

proposed_destination.reason: Probing capabilities up front turns AE version surprises into doctor failures.

text: Shape-path keyframes interpolate a normalised 0-1 progress, so ease speed on a path is 1/T; AE also invalidates sibling property references after addProperty, so re-resolve them after every add.

proposed_destination.reason: Both behaviours produced wrong eases or dead references until the helpers encoded them.

text: Before any AE mutation, probe which project is open, whether it's dirty and what's in the render queue.

proposed_destination.reason: The preflight is what makes 'never discard user work' enforceable.

text: Purge AE's RAM caches before a long aerender (this doesn't touch the disk cache).

proposed_destination.reason: Stale RAM caches add memory pressure to the render.

text: The ES3 library covers film-time snapping with the sample bias, eases converted to AE speed and influence with read-back, a settle-spring expression, shapes, text with per-character reveals, tabular counters, imports, plate layers, placeholders and a prefs-based report channel; brand tokens, fonts and names come from config.

proposed_destination.reason: It mirrors the Remotion kit so both engines share one motion law.

text: Interpret generated plates at their native frame rate in AE, use Pixel Motion blending only on slow drifts, never add AE motion blur to them, and regenerate fast generated motion rather than time-stretching it.

proposed_destination.reason: Stretched generated motion smears; its blur is already baked in.

text: The AE project uses a fixed folder layout (shots, acts, master, plates, audio, code renders) and tags every shot comp RENDERED, BUILT or PLACEHOLDER.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner can open the project and see at a glance what's final.

text: Native AE act builders (event-timed carriers from the film clock) proved AE can build scenes; they were superseded for one film but are the basis for AE-built acts.

proposed_destination.reason: The pattern, not the content, carries into Slate's second engine.

text: The master queue script reads each chunk's span back in frames and flags any mismatch before rendering.

proposed_destination.reason: A wrong span is cheap to catch before a render and expensive after.

text: Nothing runs alongside aerender: conform each chunk after its pass, verify its frames, then delete the 4444 intermediate.

proposed_destination.reason: Parallel work starves aerender of memory, which is what aborts long renders.

text: The disk watchdog stops only its own aerender, not every aerender on the machine (pkill -f aerender killed them all).

proposed_destination.reason: Another job's render shouldn't die because this one ran low on disk.

text: Shape layers default to an origin at the comp centre; set anchor and position to the centre to write comp-space vertices.

proposed_destination.reason: Otherwise every vertex lands offset by half the comp.

text: AE's launch-time dialogs (licence or sign-in, the Home screen, crash-recovery restore, missing fonts or footage on open) sit outside beginSuppressDialogs and can hang unattended runs; doctor detects them.

proposed_destination.reason: An unattended job waiting on a dialog looks like a hang, not an error.

text: Adobe Media Encoder comes with AE and the bridge can queue to it, but the pipeline doesn't need it.

proposed_destination.reason: Keeping AME out of the path avoids its separate licence limits on automation.

text: Doctor for AE checks presence and version, the aerender path, Automation permission, the scripting pref state, disk-cache state and free space, fonts from the brand pack, ffmpeg capabilities, Node and Remotion, the OCR engine, the Whisper model, MCP registration, and a live ae_project_info when the pref is on.

proposed_destination.reason: Each item was a real failure or a manual check during the films.

text: Masters run with a preflight (AE GUI closed, disk cache off, free space of at least a few times the estimate) and a postflight (cache restored, manifest written last).

proposed_destination.reason: Templated preflight and postflight make the fragile steps repeatable.

text: The AE bridge's project export and import use its own JSON schema, not Lottie; HTML-to-scene, cloud preview and a Lottie converter aren't provided.

proposed_destination.reason: Assuming Lottie interop would send builders down a dead end.

text: The vendor's AE panel and its cloud bridge generate footage into an AE project (CEP-based), a different route from the local bridge Slate uses; their automation targets repeated structured assignments, not complex character animation.

proposed_destination.reason: Knowing each route's scope stops the wrong one being picked.

text: aerender renders without the AE interface; in Render-Only mode it reportedly doesn't need an Adobe sign-in (medium confidence).

proposed_destination.reason: Sign-in state matters for unattended master renders.

text: aerender ignores its render-settings, output-module, output and range flags unless -comp is given.

proposed_destination.reason: Masters render queue items (-rqindex), so their settings live in the saved project.

text: aerender's -mfr ON|OFF max_cpu_percent toggles Multi-Frame Rendering and caps CPU.

proposed_destination.reason: A CPU cap keeps the machine usable during masters.

text: Several aerender instances can't write one movie file; parallel AE renders output image sequences, and plugins on render nodes carry their own licences.

proposed_destination.reason: Parallel masters need a different output shape.

text: Build on ExtendScript (unaffected by Adobe's UXP move) and avoid CEP-panel routes for anything long-lived: AE's UXP beta is due by November 2026, and CEP leaves the flagship apps by December 2029.

proposed_destination.reason: Community MCPs built on CEP panels have a known end date.

text: Community AE MCP servers (CEP-panel based, MIT) and nexrender (data-driven templates via aerender) exist as untested fallbacks.

proposed_destination.reason: If the bridge fails, Slate falls back to its own ExtendScript library first.

text: Adobe's own AI (the in-app AE assistant, the Claude connector) can't drive After Effects; connecting to AE means a local bridge plus aerender.

proposed_destination.reason: There's no first-party shortcut to wait for.

text: After Effects steps start only on a person's go: Adobe's PSLT section 1.2 bars operations no individual user initiated (automated server processing, RPA) unless a Sales Order allows it, so autonomous mode never touches AE.

proposed_destination.reason: The enterprise terms are the rule until the owner's own licence terms are checked.

text: The consumer General Terms for individual Creative Cloud subscriptions weren't reviewed; the PSLT rule applies until they are. Unlimited Render Engines are allowed on an intranet with one full AE install, and Media Encoder can't serve as a hosted encoder.

proposed_destination.reason: The open question is recorded so it gets checked, not assumed.

text: Never add output-module templates to the owner's AE preferences; the only preference Slate changes is the disk-cache toggle (with AE closed, restored afterwards) through the byte-safe prefs tool.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner's AE setup is theirs; a text-mode prefs rewrite once reset every preference.

text: The AE bridge's clean-rig references (one of them shaped the films' visual-foundation process) are worth reading through ae_get_skill during look development.

proposed_destination.reason: They're served by the bridge, never copied, and still useful as craft reading.

text: Per-shot QA evidence: a half-res preview with sound, every frame +-10 around each cut as a strip, full-res detail frames at each timeline event (landing + 20 frames), and a motion scan.

proposed_destination.reason: This evidence is what a human reviews and what defect reports cite.

text: Record each shot's QA status as pass, fixed -> pass, fail or pending, with notes; a human looks at the contact sheets and strips.

proposed_destination.reason: OCR and scanners can't judge everything (logos, taste); the status table makes the human pass explicit.

text: Film validation reports PASS, FAIL or REVIEW per check with evidence; nothing unchecked is ever reported as passed.

proposed_destination.reason: A quiet pass on an unrun check is how defects ship; UNCHECKED and STALE exist for that reason.

text: Log every defect with measured evidence (for example a 17.8 px jump at frame 1166, or a join jump of 1.36 against 0.13) and its fix, and move the shot's status to fixed -> pass.

proposed_destination.reason: Measured defects can be re-checked; 'looks off' can't.

text: Validation report template: check, result and evidence per row, with a detail section for each failure.

proposed_destination.reason: The report doubles as the delivery gate spec.

text: One banned-word list per brand is enforced at every layer: the script gate, a text and OCR scan of every asset, OCR of renders every 0.5 s, the captions and the Whisper transcript; an offending brand asset is quarantined.

proposed_destination.reason: Enforcing it only in the script let banned words slip in through assets and generated plates.

text: A frame-glitch scanner flags smooth fast motion (anything over about 3 px/frame); build triage into the check with a ratio test or motion-compensated matching, and skip flags within +-3 frames of a planned beat.

proposed_destination.reason: Without triage the scanner raised 1,442 flags on one film and buried the real glitches.

text: Every validator takes the film folder and reads only that film's files; one film's first validation read another film's captions and old cue sheets.

proposed_destination.reason: Defaults to another film's files produce confident, wrong results.

text: A read-time checker needs the drawn text: 9 of 10 failures on one film were checker faults (lockups, tiny labels, OCR misreading a logo). Set the storyboard's on-screen text to what's actually drawn, forgive one garbled first word, and send logo lockups to contact-sheet review.

proposed_destination.reason: OCR can't read logos; a checker that fails on them trains people to ignore it.

text: Read-time gate on the master: OCR every 0.25 s at full output width finds each on-screen statement inside its shot (+-0.5 s) and measures its longest legible run (at least 90% opacity and under 8 px/frame of motion); it must hold >= max(1.5 s, 0.4 s + 0.3 s x words) with one OCR interval of slack (fuzzy match >= 0.9).

proposed_destination.reason: Only OCR timing on the master found real faults (a line held 2.75 s of 3.1 s; a lockup got about 1 s); storyboard estimates missed them.

text: Read-time extras: numbers hold at least 2.0 s after the count lands, labels of three words or fewer hold at least 1.0 s, and a line matched to the VO stays until the VO has said it.

proposed_destination.reason: Numbers need extra time to register; VO-matched text leaving early reads as a mistake.

text: Motion-scan gate: a frame-difference spike (over max(8, 6 x (median + 0.5)) and 2.5x both neighbours) that isn't within +-3 frames of a planned event or a shot edge is flagged for review.

proposed_destination.reason: Planned events explain most spikes; the rest are the pops a human needs to see.

text: Cuts gate: no hard cuts or crossfades between shots; allowed boundaries are a carry, portal, mask, motion-masked whip, a UI state cut with the camera locked, or at most three cuts on musical hits; a detected scene change (ffmpeg scene > 0.33) must sit within 3 frames of a shot start whose transition allows it, else REVIEW.

proposed_destination.reason: Hard cuts made the reference film feel like a deck; every boundary is designed.

text: Join gate: across every act join, the jump must not exceed the largest frame step within 10 frames either side plus 1.0 (mean absolute difference, 0-255); contract holds are at least 6 still frames each side and boundary frames differ by at most a 1 px settle; a gap or overlap fails.

proposed_destination.reason: Five of five joins passed this way on one film (0.09, 0.39, 0.01, 0.02, 0.00).

text: Glitch gate: score each 16x9 tile at 480x270 luma as min(d(n-1,n), d(n,n+1)) - d(n-1,n+1)/2 and flag frames over 6.0 (plus a two-frame variant) on every render, then triage.

proposed_destination.reason: One- and two-frame pops, vanishing surfaces and z-order flips slip past per-shot review.

text: Master fidelity gate: every master frame is at least 40 dB PSNR against the act render it came from, with an exact frame count (one film averaged 56.5 dB, worst 51.6 dB).

proposed_destination.reason: Only this frame-by-frame comparison caught the colour shift and the one-frame lag.

text: Media gate: ProRes 422 HQ and H.264 masters at the film's size and fps, exact frame count, with audio present.

proposed_destination.reason: The masters are checked as files, not assumed from the render settings.

text: Captions gate: text reproduces the script exactly; at most 2 lines of 42 characters; each cue at least 1.0 s; never overlapping; shown from its first word to its last word plus 0.35 s.

proposed_destination.reason: Captions built from word timings and checked against the script are accessible and exact.

text: Spoken-words gate: Whisper (model recorded in the evidence) on the final mix against the booth script, under 5% unmatched else REVIEW, the brand name heard in full as many times as scripted, and no banned words in the transcript.

proposed_destination.reason: One film matched 623 of 631 words, the rest digits and spelling; the gate proves the mix says what the script says.

text: QA tools read the brand word, banned list, targets and film folder from the brand pack and film.json; the films hard-coded one brand's words, a reference runtime and film switches.

proposed_destination.reason: Brand constants in QA code make every other brand fail or pass wrongly.

text: One film's last validation showed word-landing failures (93 beats, worst 469.7 ms) with its re-master pending.

proposed_destination.reason: A status of one film at reading time, not a lesson; the gates that caught it are harvested.

text: The GPU renderer isn't bit-exact run to run (about 1 level, 66 dB): a frame counts as changed only if it differs from both of two baseline renders, and a react-dom/server markup diff works as a no-browser check.

proposed_destination.reason: Pixel gates without the rule flag noise as change.

text: Record the Whisper model in every gate's evidence (turbo for per-take timing, large-v3-turbo for the final transcript).

proposed_destination.reason: Different models hear differently; a result without its model can't be compared.

text: Delete OCR frames once their JSON is cached (keyed by file size and mtime), and delete verified intermediates (4444 chunks, chunk files) straight away.

proposed_destination.reason: OCR and chunk intermediates are the quiet disk hogs.

text: A quick validation mode skips the slow checks (read-time OCR, Whisper) for iteration, but only a full run can pass delivery.

proposed_destination.reason: Whisper on a long mix is slow; iteration needs speed, delivery needs completeness.

text: The loudness check must actually gate 24-bit output: an operator-precedence bug left its result unused, so bit depth was reported but never gated.

proposed_destination.reason: One of the four known validator bugs the plan requires regression tests for.

text: Treat a stem at or below -69.9 LUFS, or with no true peak, as silent: ebur128 floors silence at -70.0, so a '< -70' test never fired and an empty ambience stem passed.

proposed_destination.reason: A silent stem is either intended (declare it) or a failure; the check has to see it.

text: One OCR engine (Apple Vision through the Python environment) serves every gate; when it's unavailable the gate is UNCHECKED, never a quiet pass from another engine.

proposed_destination.reason: Two OCR engines were in use; switching engines silently changes results.
