text: Vision's accurate recognition may be missing its model assets; doctor checks which level is available and gates record the level they used.

proposed_destination.reason: The fast level misreads more; evidence must say which ran.

text: OCR runs on full-output-width frames only; at 1280 px it misread letter-spaced capitals (an 'I' read as a '1', a 'B' as an '8').

proposed_destination.reason: Downscaled OCR produced false banned-word and read-time results.

text: The owner's ponder skill (converging grading passes) can run as a QA loop over every shot.

proposed_destination.reason: An optional dependency for a thorough review pass.

text: Freeze, flash and blank-frame metrics (as in video-verifier's analyzer) belong in Slate's QA beside the glitch scan.

proposed_destination.reason: They overlap the glitch scan but catch different faults.

text: Captions stay at or under 17 characters per second (Netflix's children's limit; 20 for adults), with each caption event between 5/6 s and 7 s.

proposed_destination.reason: Two lines of 42 characters says nothing about speed; cps does.

text: On-screen text never straddles a cut.

proposed_destination.reason: Text that survives a cut reads as a mistake and breaks read-time measurement.

text: Keep titles inside title-safe (90% of the frame: 1728x972 at 1080p, 96 px in from the sides and 54 px from top and bottom) and action inside 93%; social formats add their platform safe zones.

proposed_destination.reason: Platform UI covers the edges of social frames; broadcast crops them.

text: At most three flashes a second (WCAG 2.3.1).

proposed_destination.reason: Flashes above that rate are a seizure risk.

text: Building the Vision OCR helper from Swift source at install.

proposed_destination.reason: Superseded: the plan keeps one OCR engine (ocrmac through uv) and drops the Swift binary.

text: The validation report's check table doubles as the delivery gate spec.

proposed_destination.reason: One list defines both what's checked and what's delivered.

text: Events gate: every act in shots.json has a valid events file or an explicit silent flag with a reason; one film's first two acts had no events file, yet its sync check passed.

proposed_destination.reason: A missing events file means a silent act that every other check misses.

text: The banned-word list is defined once per brand and imported by every check; one validator kept its own copy of the list, which could drift from the script gate's.

proposed_destination.reason: One of the four known validator bugs the plan requires regression tests for.

text: The act-join check runs on any film's renders; the source tool was hard-wired to one film.

proposed_destination.reason: One of the four known validator bugs the plan requires regression tests for.

text: Contact sheets every 0.5 s, labelled with timecode, are made straight from the act renders.

proposed_destination.reason: They show the whole film at a glance without waiting for masters.

text: Delivery includes the masters, stems, captions, a SHA-256 manifest of every deliverable (missing ones listed), review and phone cuts, contact sheets, a rebuild runbook, an asset ledger with provenance and spend, and QA records.

proposed_destination.reason: A delivery someone else can verify and rebuild is the bar, not just a video file.

text: Make share-size copies for the owner as part of delivery: a full H.264, a copy small enough for chat (about 70 MB) and a phone copy.

proposed_destination.reason: The films made these by hand every time; they belong in the delivery list.

text: When more than one mix exists, an audio README states which one is the delivery.

proposed_destination.reason: One film's delivery audio was a copy of the v2 mix sitting beside the archived v1 mix; without the note nobody could tell.

text: Review cuts at every stage: voice-only previews, per-shot half-res previews with sound, whole-film half-res and phone cuts with contact sheets straight from act renders, and side-by-side comparisons (code versus generated, alternative versus flagship).

proposed_destination.reason: The owner reviews early and often without waiting for masters.

text: Rebuild runbook template: tools and versions, locked inputs not to regenerate, picture per act, sound, AE and masters, and checks; a film must rebuild from its folder with no paid generation.

proposed_destination.reason: One film was fully rebuildable from saved inputs; that's the bar for every delivery.

text: Never mux with ffmpeg -shortest: it cut the last 4 frames because the mix was 9 microseconds short; write mixes exactly picture length and verify frame counts after every mux.

proposed_destination.reason: Lost frames at the end of a master are easy to miss and impossible to excuse.

text: Output names (masters, captions, review cuts, manifests) derive from the film id, not a hard-coded film name.

proposed_destination.reason: The films' tools wrote one brand's file names for every film.

text: Contact sheets, burst sheets and labelled sheets use a bundled or configured font, never a macOS system font path.

proposed_destination.reason: System font paths break on other machines and other operating systems.

text: Formats carry their loudness target (web about -14 LUFS, broadcast -23 or -24 LUFS) instead of one hard-coded target.

proposed_destination.reason: The films had no broadcast profile; any other destination needs one.

text: Join master chunks by stream copy (H.264 chunks start on an IDR frame; ProRes is intra-only), then mux the final mix once: AAC 320 kb/s at 48 kHz with faststart for H.264, 24-bit PCM for ProRes.

proposed_destination.reason: Stream-copy joins are lossless and fast; one mux keeps audio exact.

text: Review cut: 960x540 at about 3 Mb/s with 192k AAC; phone cut: 640x360 at about 450 kb/s with 96k AAC and under 30 MB; contact sheets: a frame every 0.5 s at 480x270, 12x10 per sheet, labelled m:ss.s.

proposed_destination.reason: These sizes worked for review on a phone and in chat; the hardware encoder used is macOS-only, so a portable fallback is needed.

text: Write the delivery manifest last: it hashes files, so anything regenerated after it (a validation report, for example) leaves a stale hash.

proposed_destination.reason: One film's manifest hashed a validation report that was rewritten 16 minutes later.

text: The manifest lists every deliverable with bytes, SHA-256 and an ffprobe summary, and lists missing ones instead of skipping them.

proposed_destination.reason: A manifest that skips missing files hides an incomplete delivery.

text: Never edit a shell script while a job runs it: zsh reads scripts incrementally and a job failed at its last line; run jobs from a copied, versioned script.

text: Record the character-cost response header of every ElevenLabs call in the ledger.

proposed_destination.reason: Measured times seed the queue's estimates and the owner's expectations.

proposed_destination.reason: A core lane on a fast-moving, opaque dependency needs its own tests.

text: Other video toolkits and frameworks reviewed (a Claude Code video toolkit, motion-canvas, revideo, an index of video skills) aren't needed.

proposed_destination.reason: Reviewed as alternatives; Remotion, AE and the web renderer cover the engines.

text: Never copy OpenMontage code: it's AGPL-3.0 and would force AGPL on Slate; ideas only.

proposed_destination.reason: Copyleft code in the core would change Slate's licence.

text: Agents' knowledge cutoffs (GPT-6 Astra April 2026, Opus 5.5 June 2026) predate the current voice model, Remotion's newest blur, the generation vendor's API and the AE bridge, so skills state current model ids and versions from a dated registry.

proposed_destination.reason: An agent will otherwise use the models it remembers.

text: A Claude Code plugin's manifest is optional; only a kebab-case name is required and it namespaces every component; components (skills, agents, hooks, .mcp.json, workflows and more) sit at the plugin root, and a CLAUDE.md there isn't loaded, so instructions go in skills.

proposed_destination.reason: The plugin layout decides where Slate's front-door instructions can live.

text: Unknown top-level plugin.json keys are stripped with a warning, but an unknown key inside userConfig, channels, lspServers or monitors is an error and the plugin doesn't load.

proposed_destination.reason: A typo in a nested key disables the whole plugin silently for users.

text: In plugin.json, some component keys replace the default folder scan (commands, agents, workflows), skills adds to it, and hooks and MCP servers merge with the default files.

proposed_destination.reason: Declaring a key can hide the default folder's contents.

text: Plugin paths must start with ./ and stay inside the plugin; '..', symlinks that leave the plugin and backslashes are rejected.

proposed_destination.reason: A symlinked skill that points outside the plugin would be dropped from the cache.

text: Never write state under the plugin root: it changes on every update and old versions are deleted after 14 days; state, caches and environments live in the plugin data directory or Slate's own data folder.

proposed_destination.reason: Anything written there vanishes on the next update.

text: Plugin path variables are substituted in hooks, MCP and LSP config and skill bodies, but not exported to commands the Bash tool runs.

proposed_destination.reason: Scripts can't rely on those variables at run time.

text: Plugin userConfig secrets land in the Keychain, but the dialog appears only in the interactive /plugin panel (shell installs need --config, Cowork never prompts) and sensitive values never reach skill text; Slate keeps keys in its own resolver and slate connect instead.

proposed_destination.reason: One resolver across every agent beats a Claude-only secret store.

text: Plugin MCP servers connect automatically at session start and are named plugin:<plugin>:<server>, with tools named mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool> for permission rules.

proposed_destination.reason: Slate's recommended allowlist uses those names.

text: Remote MCP URLs and headers in .mcp.json expand credential variables as empty; never pass keys that way.

proposed_destination.reason: A key that silently expands to nothing looks like an auth failure.

text: Slate's MCP tools return file paths and short summaries, never frames or long logs: Claude Code warns at 10k tokens and spills results over about 25k to a file.

proposed_destination.reason: Media dumps blow the context and the tool limit.

text: MCP server precedence in Claude Code runs local, project, user, plugin, then claude.ai connectors.

proposed_destination.reason: A user-scope registration would shadow the plugin's copy of the same server.

text: Never ship a top-level bin/ in the plugin: claude.ai and Cowork refuse the whole plugin, and in Claude Code bin/ reaches only the Bash tool's PATH; the CLI reaches PATH through install.sh, and plugin helpers live in scripts/.

proposed_destination.reason: One folder name would make the plugin uninstallable on two of three surfaces.

text: The <claude-code-hint> install prompt from a CLI works only for plugins in official Anthropic marketplaces.

proposed_destination.reason: Not usable from a self-hosted marketplace, so Slate doesn't rely on it.

text: Claude Code's automatic plugin dependency install (npm ci with scripts off, a 60 s timeout, a lockfile required, yarn and pnpm skipped) can't carry Remotion, Chrome or Whisper; heavy runtimes install through doctor --install into Slate's data folder.

proposed_destination.reason: The engine and models are hundreds of megabytes and need install scripts.

text: Plugin workflows run as /<plugin>:<name>, can't import modules or touch the filesystem (agents do the work), and cap at 16 concurrent agents and 1,000 per run.

proposed_destination.reason: A make-film workflow has to delegate every file operation to agents.

text: Plugin agents ignore permissionMode, hooks, mcpServers and initialPrompt in their frontmatter.

proposed_destination.reason: Plugin agent definitions can't carry their own permissions or servers.

text: Plugin install scopes are user, project, local and managed (local wins over project over user; managed overrides all), and cloud sessions don't load local plugins or ~/.claude/skills.

proposed_destination.reason: The owner installs at user scope; cloud routines need the account-level skill.

text: A marketplace entry's name and the plugin manifest's name must be identical, or installs break.

proposed_destination.reason: A mismatch only shows up when someone tries to install.

text: A URL-hosted marketplace.json can't use relative-path plugin sources, because only the JSON file is downloaded.

proposed_destination.reason: Slate's marketplace is a git repo so relative sources work.

text: Release policy: omit the version while iterating so updates track the commit; once others depend on Slate, bump plugin.json's version per release and tag it; never set the version in both plugin.json and the marketplace entry (plugin.json silently wins).

proposed_destination.reason: A pinned version freezes users until someone remembers to bump it.

text: Plugin auto-update is off by default for third-party marketplaces; the README tells users to turn it on.

proposed_destination.reason: Without it, users never receive fixes.

text: CI runs claude plugin validate --strict and skills-ref validate on every skill.

proposed_destination.reason: Manifest and frontmatter drift across clients is caught before users see it.

text: Trigger evals run through claude plugin eval with mocked vendor MCP tools, so they cost model calls but no vendor credits.

proposed_destination.reason: Routing and triggering are tested without spending money.

text: Account-installed plugins sync into Claude Code as <name>@synced, but a plugin installed from the command line isn't added to the account.

proposed_destination.reason: Installing locally doesn't give chat the skills; the knowledge upload does.

text: Publishing to Anthropic's plugin directory needs a README of at least 40 words and a licence; organization sync needs a private or internal repo.

proposed_destination.reason: Relevant when Slate goes public.

text: Chat copies a skill's whole folder into its sandbox, so script paths stay relative to SKILL.md, and credentials never go in a skill.

proposed_destination.reason: A key inside a skill folder is uploaded with it.

text: claude.ai uploads accept only six frontmatter fields (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools) and fail hard on anything else; the zip's top level must be the skill folder, and the folder name must equal a lowercase, hyphenated name.

proposed_destination.reason: A Claude-only key like argument-hint breaks the upload for every chat user.

text: Slate's desktop extension is an .mcpb bundle (a zip with manifest.json, node server type since Node ships with Claude Desktop), handed out directly or shipped inside the plugin, because Anthropic's directory no longer accepts MCPB submissions.

proposed_destination.reason: Chat's only way to start local renders is this extension.

text: Skills load in three tiers (about 100 tokens of metadata at startup, a SKILL.md body under 5,000 tokens and 500 lines on activation, references on demand), with references one level deep and relative paths.

proposed_destination.reason: Oversized skills cost context on every activation.

text: Anthropic released Agent Skills as an open standard; Claude, Codex and ChatGPT, OpenClaw, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot and others read it, and project skills override user skills on a name clash.

proposed_destination.reason: Spec-pure skills are the one format every target reads.

text: Every Slate command is agent-safe: never interactive, --help everywhere, JSON on stdout and diagnostics on stderr, distinct exit codes, idempotent with --dry-run, bounded output (harnesses truncate around 10-30K characters), and pinned one-off tools.

proposed_destination.reason: Agents drive the CLI; anything interactive or unbounded breaks them.

text: Codex extras (display metadata, implicit-invocation policy, MCP dependencies) live in each skill's agents/openai.yaml, generated by slate skills build and ignored by other clients.

proposed_destination.reason: Client extras beside the skill keep shared frontmatter spec-pure.

text: Codex caps its skill list at 2% of context (8,000 characters), Claude Code truncates description plus when_to_use at 1,536 characters, and the spec caps descriptions at 1,024; Slate keeps about ten skills with tight descriptions.

proposed_destination.reason: Every enabled skill's description is paid for on every turn.

text: Codex and ChatGPT plugins use a root plugin.json (the Agent Plugins schema) with skills/ and mcp.json, fall back to .codex-plugin/plugin.json, and install from marketplaces (including a legacy-compatible read of .claude-plugin/marketplace.json).

proposed_destination.reason: One repo can serve Claude and Codex marketplaces at once.

text: Add OpenClaw gating (metadata.openclaw.requires for bins and env) only after skills-ref validate and a test claude.ai upload accept nested metadata, since the spec defines metadata as string-to-string.

proposed_destination.reason: Gating that breaks the claude.ai upload costs more than it gives.

text: Publish to ClawHub (OpenClaw's public registry) only if Slate's core goes public.

proposed_destination.reason: A public registry is the wrong place for a private core.

text: Never put pipeline-critical logic in hooks: OpenClaw detects Claude hooks but doesn't run them, and chat ignores them.

proposed_destination.reason: A step that only runs in one client isn't a pipeline step.

text: Launch Slate's MCP server by a plain command name (slate mcp) so no path placeholder is needed; whether OpenClaw expands ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in a Claude bundle is unverified.

proposed_destination.reason: A placeholder that one client leaves literal breaks the server there.

text: The skills CLI installs one repo into many agents by symlinking a canonical copy (-g with an -a per agent), discovers skills declared in .claude-plugin manifests, and records installs in ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json.

proposed_destination.reason: Useful for third-party skills; Slate's own skills are symlinked by install.sh.

text: Run the skills CLI with DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 (telemetry is on by default), and expect it to wipe lock files from older format versions.

proposed_destination.reason: Defaults send usage data and can erase a lock file.

text: Commit a project skills-lock.json so another machine restores the identical skill set.

proposed_destination.reason: A lock file makes the owner's agent setup reproducible.

text: Agent Plugins 1.0 is a vendor-neutral format (root plugin.json, skills/, mcp.json; MCP and skills only) read by Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot and OpenClaw but not documented for Claude Code, so Slate ships both manifests; OpenClaw prefers the .claude-plugin marker when both exist.

proposed_destination.reason: Both manifests over one skills folder reach every target.

text: In Agent Plugins' mcp.json, the stdio command takes no interpolation, and the plugin root and data placeholders work only in args, env and cwd.

proposed_destination.reason: Generated per-client configs must respect each format's placeholder rules.

text: Generate every client's manifest (Claude plugin.json and .mcp.json, Agent Plugins plugin.json and mcp.json, Codex agents/openai.yaml, the MCPB manifest) from one source definition, and fail CI when a generated copy drifts.

proposed_destination.reason: Hand-maintained manifests for five clients would drift within a week.

text: Claude's plugin cache copies only the plugin folder, so the plugin can't reach the CLI by a relative path; the CLI is installed separately and called by name.

proposed_destination.reason: A relative path to ../src works in the repo and breaks in the cache.

text: The owner adds Slate's marketplace from the local checkout so edits load in place with no version bumps; everyone else adds it from the private GitHub repo.

proposed_destination.reason: Fast iteration for the owner, versioned releases for everyone else.

text: Bundle the generation and voice vendors' remote MCP servers in the plugin's .mcp.json as http servers with OAuth (they appear on claude.ai's Connectors tab), and never put API keys in the file.

proposed_destination.reason: Chat users get the connectors with the plugin; keys stay out of the repo.

text: Claude-only extras (plugin agents for directing, sound and QA, a make-film workflow, validation hooks) are conveniences; every pipeline step also works from the CLI, because other agents ignore them.

proposed_destination.reason: Codex and OpenClaw must lose nothing essential.

text: Write script and reference paths relative to the skill root, with one line saying so, and never use client-specific placeholders (${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}, {baseDir}) in shared skill text, since other clients show them literally.

proposed_destination.reason: Shared text has to read correctly in every client.

text: Slate's MCP server is a thin, local stdio server over the CLI with coarse, job-based tools (start a render and get a job id, poll a job, list artifacts), so long renders never block a call.

proposed_destination.reason: Renders take minutes to hours; a blocking tool call would time out.

text: Remote MCP type names differ by client (http in Claude's .mcp.json, streamable-http in Agent Plugins, a transport key in OpenClaw, a url in Codex TOML), so each client's config is generated separately.

proposed_destination.reason: One shared config file can't serve all four.

text: Keep media out of the plugin (fonts, sound banks, LUTs): claude.ai caps a plugin at 200 MB and 5,000 files, files outside the plugin folder aren't copied, and Git LFS files arrive as pointers.

proposed_destination.reason: Heavy or licensed media is fetched or built at runtime instead.

text: Private marketplaces use the user's git credentials and never prompt; GITHUB_TOKEN alone doesn't authenticate (run gh auth setup-git), and background updates fail quietly.

proposed_destination.reason: A private repo install that silently stops updating looks like a bug in Slate.

text: Plugin and marketplace names are permanent and kebab-case; reserved names (npm, github, inline, synced, claudeai-*) and anything that impersonates Anthropic are refused; use displayName or renames instead of changing a name.

proposed_destination.reason: Renaming a published plugin breaks every install.

text: Five install behaviours are unverified and need a hands-on test before Slate relies on them: OpenClaw's placeholder expansion in Claude bundles, Codex reading Claude-style marketplace sources, nested OpenClaw metadata passing upload and validation, validate accepting both manifests, and which state dir the gateway uses.

proposed_destination.reason: Each is a plausible failure on a real agent; a test settles it cheaply.

text: Point skills at the vendor's live docs (llms.txt) instead of shipping a docs mirror, which goes stale.

proposed_destination.reason: A 75-file snapshot was already out of date.

text: Ship a recommended permission allowlist per agent (ffmpeg, ffprobe, Python, node renders, aerender, Whisper and slate itself) so unattended runs don't stall on prompts.

proposed_destination.reason: A detached job waiting on a permission prompt never finishes.

text: Orchestration scripts are portable Python with paths from film.json; the films' render and sound queues were zsh-only with hard-coded build folders.

proposed_destination.reason: zsh path idioms and fixed folders tie the pipeline to one Mac and one film.

text: The engine's pinned packages: remotion and its @remotion packages at 4.0.521, React 19.2.8, TypeScript 5.9.3, and three with @react-three/fiber and drei only for optional 3D, with esbuild declared.

proposed_destination.reason: The pins that rendered the films are the parity baseline.

text: A plugin skill at skills/<name>/SKILL.md runs as /<plugin>:<name>; its frontmatter name replaces the last segment, and the bare name also works when nothing else uses it.

proposed_destination.reason: Skill names are how agents and users invoke Slate.

text: A marketplace.json needs a name, an owner and a plugins list; each entry needs a name and a source (a relative path, GitHub, a git URL or subdirectory, npm, an archive or a command).

proposed_destination.reason: Slate's marketplace uses a relative-path source from its own repo.

text: Users add a marketplace with /plugin marketplace add owner/repo (or a git URL, local path or marketplace URL) and install with /plugin install <plugin>@<marketplace>; the shell forms take --scope.

proposed_destination.reason: The install instructions for anyone but the owner.

text: During development, load the plugin for one session with --plugin-dir (or --plugin-url, or CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS) and apply edits with /reload-plugins.

proposed_destination.reason: A fast loop for testing plugin changes without reinstalling.

text: Buying Remotion company seats now (the inventory's recommendation for company use).

proposed_destination.reason: Superseded by decision 5: free for now while the owner is the only operator of unpublished pilots; revisit before a company film is published.
